chunks.title: Bookkeep contractor payments made outside of Wave
chunks.content:
If you pay contractors outside of Wave, you need to manually mark the contractor bills you create as paid.
To do so, categorize the withdrawal transaction as a payment sent for a bill in Wave. This links the transaction to the bill. To categorize the withdrawal transaction as a bill payment:
Open the Transactions page.
Locate the contractor payment expense transaction.
Select the Category field, then select Payment Sent for a Bill in Wave.
Select the outstanding bill to apply the payment to.
Select Save.

chunks.title: Automatic bookkeeping when paying contractors via direct deposit
chunks.content:
If you use direct deposit to pay contractors and connect your bank account to import transactions, Wave automates the bookkeeping as explained below. Automatic bank transaction imports are part of the Pro Plan. If your transactions are not importing automatically, create a manual transfer to ensure your bookkeeping is accurate.
When you pay contractor bills using direct deposit through Wave’s payroll feature, Wave takes care of the bookkeeping automatically. This happens in three steps.
1: Wave creates a liability
When you create a bill for your contractor, Wave creates a liability in your accounts payable. You can view this in your reports.
2: Wave marks the bill as paid
When you choose to pay a contractor by direct deposit and the approved payroll is processed, Wave creates an expense transaction on your Transactions page. This transaction is categorized as a Payment Sent for a Bill in Wave. There is a separate transaction for each bill payment, and each of these is recorded in your Wave Payroll Clearing account.
3: Wave categorizes the bank withdrawal
When the withdrawal transaction from your bank account imports into Wave, it is automatically categorized as a Transfer to Wave Payroll Clearing. This restores the balance that was withdrawn from your Wave Payroll Clearing account.
If your imported transaction wasn't categorized automatically, follow these steps.
The bill payment transactions generated for contractor payments made via payroll direct deposit cannot be edited or deleted.
Manually create a transfer to the clearing account
If the transfer transaction was not created automatically or you don't have automatic bank transaction imports, add the transfer transaction manually:
Open the Transactions page.
Find your bank-imported bill payment transaction, or create the expense transaction.
Select the category Transfer to a Bank, Credit Card or Loan > Wave Payroll Clearing. If you’re creating a new transaction, fill in the other details too.
Select Save.

chunks.title: Send a payment receipt for a recurring invoice
chunks.content:
Once your customer has paid an invoice generated from a recurring invoice, they may ask for a payment receipt as proof of purchase.
If automatic payments are turned on, your customer will be sent a receipt automatically.
With manual payments, you will need to send them the receipt yourself. To find the list of invoices generated from a recurring invoice:
On the left-side menu, click Sales & Payments > Recurring Invoices.
Click the dropdown arrow next to the recurring invoice for the specific customer.
Select View created invoices.
Once you’ve located the invoice, follow the steps from step 3 onwards in Send a receipt for an invoice payment.
If your customer would like a receipt before the payment transaction has been imported into your Wave account, follow the steps in How to provide a customer receipt before payment is recorded.
chunks.category: Help Center > Invoices & Estimates > Recurring Invoices

chunks.title: End a recurring invoice
chunks.content:
End a recurring invoice
Recurring invoices automatically end based on the date, or number of invoices set when creating the schedule. However, you may want to end the recurring invoice early. In this case, you can do so by following these steps:
On the left-side menu, click Sales & Payments > Recurring Invoices.
Click the dropdown arrow next to the recurring invoice you want to end.
Select End.
After you end a recurring invoice, you can’t reactivate it. Instead, you can duplicate it. Click the dropdown arrow next to the recurring invoice, then select Duplicate to create a new recurring invoice.
You can't delete recurring invoices or recurring invoice drafts.
chunks.category: Help Center > Invoices & Estimates > Recurring Invoices

chunks.title: Unmerge transactions
chunks.content:
If you have a Pro Plan or Receipts subscription, Wave automatically merges some duplicate transactions. Learn more in Automated bookkeeping with auto-updates.
If unmerging a transaction will affect a completed reconciliation period, a warning pop-up will appear. Learn how to fix an unreconciled period.
Unmerge transactions in your web browser
Unmerge transactions in the mobile app
Unmerge transactions in your web browser
On the left-side menu, click Accounting > Transactions.
At the far right of the transaction, click the dropdown arrow, then Edit more details.
Scroll down to the bottom of the pop-up and click Merged transactions or Automerge.
In the next pop-up, click Unmerge.
This unmerges the transactions, and the original two transactions become visible on your Transactions page.
Unmerging a transaction may affect that account's reconciliation periods. Check the account’s reconciliation status to ensure everything is still accurate.
Unmerge transactions in the mobile app
In the bottom menu, tap Accounting > Transactions.
Locate and tap on the merged transaction to open it.
At the bottom of the transaction details, tap Merged transactions or Review merge.
In the merged transactions' details screen, tap Unmerge.
This unmerges the transactions, and the original two transactions become visible on your Transactions page.
Unmerging a transaction may affect that account's reconciliation periods. Log in on a web browser to review the account’s reconciliation status.

chunks.title: Set a default business
chunks.content:
When you create a Wave account, Wave automatically chooses a default business to load when you log in. To change which business profile Wave loads first, select a default:
Click on your business name in the top right corner, then Profile settings.
Select Businesses in the Profile menu.
Click the star icon beside the business you want to make the default.
You cannot set a business you have View or Edit access to as your default.
Click Yes, make it the default business.
You will now see a Default label next to this business. You can change the default business at any time.
chunks.category: Help Center > Manage Your Account > Manage Your Profile

chunks.title: Invite or remove collaborators from your business
chunks.content:
You can grant trusted individuals, such as accountants, tax preparers, or business partners, access to your Wave account by inviting them as users. Learn about the different user types and permission levels.
When a trusted user collaborates on your Wave account, they can only see the business or personal profile they have been invited to. You must invite a user to each business individually for them to access additional business profiles.
Add a user to your business profile
Resend an invitation
User account setup
Edit or delete a user

chunks.title: Is Wave free?
chunks.content:
You can sign up for Wave for free on a web browser and on the Wave mobile app.
When signing up for Wave, you have the choice between the Starter Plan and the Pro Plan.
The Starter Plan is free and includes basic accounting and invoicing features. You can add paid features such as accepting online payments, automatic receipt scanning, and payroll.
The Pro Plan is a paid subscription and includes all the features of the Starter Plan, as well as receipt scanning, auto-import bank transactions, automatic transaction merging and categorization, and more. Learn more about Pro Plan features.
If your business needs change, you can switch plans, cancel, or reactivate a subscription at any time.

chunks.title: Why can't I change my business currency?
chunks.content:
When you create a business in Wave, a currency will be recommended based on your business location. To change the currency, click Change this during setup. Your selected currency becomes the default for your business and cannot be changed once set.
Only USD and CAD are currency options as Wave is only available to US and Canadian businesses.
Why can’t business currency be changed?
Small businesses generally report income and pay taxes in their domestic currency. If you relocate to another country, you are starting a new business. While your operations and clients may remain the same, the tax obligations and currency used are different.
If you move your business to another country, create a new business in Wave. To ensure proper compliance, consult an accountant in your original country and your new country.
For help setting up your new business, Wave has a team of in-house bookkeepers and accounting coaches. Learn more about Personalized help with Wave Advisors.
What to do if you set up the wrong currency
If you selected the wrong currency at set up, create a new business with the correct currency. Once the new business is created, archive the incorrect business to prevent confusion.

chunks.title: Account for a lump sum invoice payment
chunks.content:
To complete the steps in this article, log in to your account from a web browser at waveapps.com.
When a customer has more than one invoice due, they may make one payment for the total due rather than multiple small payments for each of their invoices. The lump sum payment transaction must be split to record a payment on each remaining outstanding invoice.
Record a lump sum invoice payment received outside of Wave
Account for a lump sum invoice payment received with Wave’s online payments
Record a lump sum invoice payment received outside of Wave
If a customer pays with a lump sum amount outside of Wave (such as with a check), split the payment transaction to account for each intended invoice.
On the left-side menu, select Accounting > Transactions.
Find the transaction for the lump sum payment. Click the dropdown arrow to the right, then select Edit more details. Or, create an income transaction and fill in the details.
To split the payment, click Split transaction, until you have a Split amount section for each paid invoice.
In each Split amount section, enter the amount paid for the related invoice.
Categorize each section as a Payment Received for an Invoice in Wave and select the relevant invoice number from the dropdown menu.
Click Save.
If the funds you received exceeds the total of all invoices, you must record the invoice overpayment(s) separately.
Account for a lump sum invoice payment received with Wave’s online payments
If a lump sum payment is made using Wave’s online payments feature, a negative amount (indicated using brackets) will appear as due on the invoice the payment was applied to. This is the amount to be recorded on the other outstanding invoices.
You need to bookkeep this overpayment to the customer's credit account before you can apply the payment to other invoices.
Each customer can have one credit account. This account is automatically created the first time you select the option to transfer funds to a customer credit account.
To do this:
chunks.category: Help Center > Accounting > Accounting for your sales

chunks.title: Account for a lump sum invoice payment
chunks.content:
On the left-side menu, click Sales & Payments > Invoices.
To the right of the overpaid invoice, select Manage overpayment.
Wave automatically enters the overpaid portion in the Amount field. You can edit the amount if needed.
In the Method field, select Transfer to customer credit account to apply to a future payment. Wave automatically selects the customer's credit account, which you cannot change.
Click Submit.
This makes the balance due on the invoice zero and credits the created lump sum account for the remainder of the funds received.
Next, you need to apply the additional paid funds to the correct invoices. This will ensure that the lump sum payment is recorded on the intended invoices.
On the left-side menu, select Sales & Payments > Invoices.
Locate one of the overdue invoices included with the lump sum and click on it.
In the Manage payments section, click Record a payment.
In the Method dropdown, click Customer credit. Wave automatically selects the customer's credit account.
Click Submit.
Repeat these steps until each invoice is recorded as paid.
If funds remain in the customer's credit account after applying payments to the invoices, you will need to account for the overpayment.

chunks.title: How to create a transfer between two accounts (e.g. categorize a credit card payment)
chunks.content:
Learn how to bookkeep transfers and credit card payments with a video.
When you move money from one bank account to another, you need to record this as a transfer. This ensures your account balances are correct, and that you won't mistake a single movement of funds between your accounts as income (or an expense).
For a transfer to take place in Wave, you will need two transactions. One transaction to show from which account the funds originated, and one to show which account the funds landed in. Examples of a transfer include:
Making a credit card payment
Making a loan repayment
Moving money from your checking to your savings account
Depositing cash into a bank account
This article details how to create transfers between accounts in the same currency. Read how to create transfers between accounts with different currencies in this article.
To create a transfer:
Open the Transactions page.
Locate one of the transactions associated with this transfer.
Categorize the transaction as Transfer to/from Bank, Credit Card, or Loan, then select the matching transaction of the other side of this transfer.
Select transfer to when categorizing a transaction under the account where the funds are received. Or, select transfer from if the transaction is under the account where the funds are sent from.
Select Save, and the transactions will change from Uncategorized to Transfer to/Transfer from.
Your reports will now correctly record this as a transfer of funds, rather than an uncategorized income or expense.
The two transactions must be located in different payment accounts, so you can show the flow of money from one account to the another.
What to do if there are no matching transactions
If you categorize a transaction as Transfer to/from Bank, Credit Card, or Loan, you may not be given the option to match with a transaction. A few possible reasons for not being given the option to match with a transaction are:
The other side of the transfer doesn’t exist in your Wave account.

chunks.title: How to create a transfer between two accounts (e.g. categorize a credit card payment)
chunks.content:
You may have the other side of the transfer located in an account not importing to Wave.
The amounts of both transactions don’t match.
The transactions are in a different currency.
The dates of the transfers are too far apart.
The other side of the transfer is already categorized.
A transfer in Wave cannot exist without both sides of the transfer being recorded, so Wave automatically creates the other transaction for you, with the description Created Transfer. This occurs when you save a transaction categorized as Transfer to/from Bank, Credit Card, or Loan, without selecting a matching transaction. This transaction will be recorded on the same date as the transaction you categorized as Transfer to/from Bank, Credit Card, or Loan, with the account being set to the account you selected in the Account dropdown.
Examples of transactions which don’t require a transfer
Sometimes you may have only one side of a transfer to record. If you are moving funds from one account in Wave, to an account that doesn’t exist in Wave, for example, a personal account, you don’t need to record this as a transfer. When this occurs, you can use the category Personal Expense/Withdrawal and then select the most suitable equity account, for example, Owner Investment/Drawings.
If you are making a payment to a vendor, this wouldn’t be categorized as a transfer either. This would be categorized as an Expense.
We highly recommend checking in with an accountant if you’re unsure of which category works best for your business when entering your transactions. Suggesting specific categories is beyond the scope that Wave can advise on.

chunks.title: Upload a bank or credit card statement in .csv format
chunks.content:
If your bank offers the option to export your data in Microsoft Money (.OFX), Quickbooks (.QBO), Quicken (.QFX) or Simply Accounting (.ASO) format, download one of those instead. All these formats are easier to import into Wave than a .CSV file; go back to your bank and re-export in one of these formats, then follow the steps in this article.
If your bank only offers .CSV imports, follow the steps below once you have downloaded the statement from your bank. Click here to download our CSV template. You can use it as a reference to format your file.
If you’re uploading a statement into a bank or credit card account that already exists in your account, follow the steps below. If not, first add a payment account under your Chart of Accounts.
On the left-side menu, click Accounting > Transactions.
Click More at the top right, then select Upload transactions.
Under Statement, click Choose File and locate the statement you downloaded from your bank to your computer.
In the Payment Account menu, select the account you want your transactions to go into.
The currency in the statement should match the currency of the payment account. If there are no currency codes in the statement, Wave will record the transactions in the currency of your payment account.
Click Upload.
On the Select date page, choose the column with the date Wave should assign to each transaction. For example, if you're uploading a bank statement, you should select the date you made the purchase (the transaction date). If you're uploading a credit card statement, you should select the date the bank took the money from the credit card (the posting date). If there is only one date column in your file, Wave will make a selection for you. Click Confirm date to continue.
chunks.category: Help Center > Transaction Imports > Transaction Imports

chunks.title: Upload a bank or credit card statement in .csv format
chunks.content:
On the Select amounts page, you'll be asked to choose the column with the amounts you either paid into or charged to your account. If you're uploading a statement for a checking account, click on the column with amounts representing deposits, such as a check you deposited. If you're uploading a statement for a credit card, click on the column with the amounts representing charges to the account, such as a purchase you made on your card. If there is only one amount column in your file, Wave will make a selection for you. Click Confirm amounts to continue. 
On the Select description page, choose the column with the best description for your transactions. This will help you identify them after they're imported into Wave. If there is only one description column in your file, Wave will make a selection for you. Click Select description to continue.
On the Confirm import page, make sure columns are highlighted correctly. If you need to change the date, amount or description columns that are highlighted, you can click on any of the Select date, Select amount or Select description headers to make your changes. 
Click Upload my statement. Transactions will import to your Transactions page.

Scheduled reminders will only be sent to the primary email associated with your customer's contact information. To send reminders to additional contacts, you will need to send them manually. To manually send a reminder, follow the steps in Send an invoice payment reminder.
To schedule invoice payment reminders on an individual invoice:

Scroll down to the Reminder settings section.
Select the checkboxes to schedule reminders. This only applies to new invoices you create. You can schedule reminders:

14, 7, and/or 3 days before the due date.

chunks.title: Introduction to debits and credits
chunks.content:
On your Transactions page, debits are green transactions, and credits are black transactions. Whether a transaction is a debit or a credit depends on whether the account is an asset or a liability.
Track your assets and liabilities on your balance sheet.
Asset accounts
Liability accounts
Transfers
Asset accounts
Assets are things that a business owns or is owed. Asset accounts include bank accounts like checking or savings, outstanding invoices, and equipment.
Deposits to asset accounts are debits, while withdrawals from accounts are credits.
Liability accounts
Liabilities are things that a business must pay or owes to others. Liability accounts include loans, credit cards, customer credits for future services, and vendor bills.
Payments made to reduce credit card or loan debts are debits, while purchases for the business are credits.
Transfers
In Wave, a transfer is when you move money from one account to another. The account the money is withdrawn from is a credit, and the account the funds are deposited into is a debit. If you move money from your checking account to pay your credit card, your checking account will be credited, and your credit card will be debited.
Learn more in How to create a transfer between two accounts.

chunks.title: How Wave keeps your bank connections secure
chunks.content:
Automatic bank transaction imports are part of Wave’s Pro Plan. Learn more about Wave’s plans or how to subscribe.
Wave partners with Plaid, a specialist provider of secure bank data connections, to offer you the ability to connect your bank accounts safely. Plaid uses best-in-class security controls to protect your data. 
Read-only security: The connection Wave makes with your financial institutions to import transactions is read-only.
Password protection: For increased security, Wave employs industry-leading online banking services to manage bank account and password data. These third parties are trusted by some of the world’s biggest banks.
Secure data transmission: Wave secures your data with up to 256-bit TLS encryption, the strength of protection you get with online banking and shopping.

chunks.title: What to do if Wave can't read your statement in CSV format
chunks.content:
If Wave cannot read your CSV file due to an error not listed in this article, try importing your transactions with Wave’s CSV template, or use Wave Connect.
Common error messages
The CSV file must contain an amount, date and description column
Wave is having difficulty reading the file you uploaded
Wave can’t find any transactions in your file
Wave is having difficulty reading the dates of your transactions
Wave is having difficulty reading the amounts of your transactions
Wave can’t find a description of your transactions
The file you provided doesn't match any format we support
File contains transactions in multiple currencies or File contains an unknown currency code
Other errors
The CSV file must contain an amount, date and description column
To import properly, your CSV file must have three or four columns:
date
amount of the transaction - all in one column, or one column each for deposits and withdrawals
description
If your CSV file is not uploading when you have separate deposit and withdrawal columns, move the amounts into a single column.
When uploading credit card transactions, purchases must be a positive amount, while payments must be negative.
Wave is having difficulty reading the file you uploaded
This error can occur for two reasons:
Your CSV file has more than four columns with inconsistent information. To resolve this error, ensure you only have columns for the transaction's date, amounts, and description. Delete any other columns.
Your CSV file name is too long. To resolve this error, rename your file something like month-year-account.csv or monthyear.csv, then re-upload it.
Wave can't find any transactions in your file
This error can occur for two reasons:
Your file contains no data. To resolve this error, ensure your file has at least one transaction.
Column titles are at the bottom of the table. To resolve this error, delete any columns without transaction information and move column titles to the top of the table.
chunks.category: Help Center > Transaction Imports > Troubleshooting Tips

chunks.title: What to do if Wave can't read your statement in CSV format
chunks.content:
Wave is having difficulty reading the dates of your transactions
This error can occur for three reasons:
There are two or more date columns, such as a transaction date and an approval date. Delete one of the columns.
There are rows with commas or blank spaces. If you have a row without relevant transaction information, delete it, then re-upload the file.
Wave cannot recognize the date’s format. The date cannot be in the future and must use this formatting:
YYYY/MM/DD or YYYY-MM-DD
Use numerical values, full month names, or 3-letter month names. For example, 2025/Jan/01
Can have 'st','nd','rd' or 'th' after day numbers. For example, 2025/January/20th
Wave is having difficulty reading the amounts of your transactions
This error can occur for three reasons:
Amounts are written in words instead of numerical values
The currency symbol in your file does not determine transaction currency. The currency will match the payment account chosen when uploading your file.
There is incorrect punctuation. Use spaces, commas, apostrophes, or decimals to indicate number values. Use brackets or the minus sign to indicate negative amounts. For example, 1 000,54 or 1.00,54
There are symbols other than the currency symbol, or the currency symbol is after the amount
If you continue to see this error, format the amount column as currency. Then, re-upload the file.
Wave can't find a description for your transactions
Your statement must have a column for the transaction’s description. The column can be empty, however, if you’re adding a description, it must contain words. A description column cannot contain only numbers.
To resolve this error, open your file and add a description column containing words.
The file you provided doesn't match any format we support
Wave supports the following file formats:
.OFX
.QBO
.QFX
.ASO
.CSV
If your file is not a CSV file, see What to do if Wave can’t read your OFX, QBO, QFX, or ASO file.
chunks.category: Help Center > Transaction Imports > Troubleshooting Tips

chunks.title: What to do if Wave can't read your statement in CSV format
chunks.content:
If your file has been saved as an .XLS file, re-save it as a .CSV (comma delimited) file instead.
Wave does not support PDF files for transaction uploads.
File contains transactions in multiple currencies or File contains an unknown currency code
This error can occur for two reasons:
There are multiple currencies in your file. To resolve this, create and upload a CSV file for each currency separately.
There is an unknown currency. To resolve this, remove any currency symbols in your file and ensure you upload to the correct currency account in Wave.
Other errors
You may receive a generic error if you have account balance totals in your file. To resolve this, remove the row that shows the balance totals.
chunks.category: Help Center > Transaction Imports > Troubleshooting Tips

chunks.title: Review your transactions
chunks.content:
Reviewing transactions is only possible on the web version of Wave.
Marking a transaction as reviewed on the Transactions page helps you ensure all the details of the transaction are correct.
You cannot review a transaction if the Category or Account fields have missing details. Fill in these fields before marking transactions as reviewed. Leaving a transaction unreviewed does not impact your reports or your ability to reconcile your account.
Reviewing a transaction is not the same as reconciling a transaction. Learn how to reconcile your books.
To mark a transaction as reviewed:
On the left-side menu, click Accounting > Transactions.
To the right of the transaction, click the checkmark icon.
Transactions that have been auto-merged or auto-categorized have an auto-updates icon in place of the checkmark icon. Learn more in Review auto-updates to your transactions.
To review several transactions at once, learn how to bulk review transactions.

chunks.title: What to do if Wave can't read your OFX, QBO, ASO, or QFX file
chunks.content:
Electronic statements have encoding that tells Wave how to upload its information. When uploading your statement, if you see the error message Wave needs you to make a small change to your file so we can read it, you may need to change your file's encoding.
To edit your file:
Open your statement in any text editor.
At the top of your file, there is an encoding line that says either ENCODING:USASCII or ENCODING:UTF-8.
If you see USASCII, change it to UTF-8.
If you see UTF-8, change it to USASCII.
Save your file.
Upload your newly saved file to Wave.
chunks.category: Help Center > Transaction Imports > Troubleshooting Tips

chunks.title: Starting balances: What they are, and how to enter them in Wave
chunks.content:
A starting balance is the amount of funds in an account at the beginning of a new fiscal period. It allows you to see the balance of the account without entering the full transaction history.
When adding a new bank account, enter the starting balance for the account at the start of your business's fiscal year.
Enter a starting balance for bank accounts, credit cards, or loans
Enter a starting balance for non-payment accounts
Starting balance when you connect your bank or credit card
Enter a starting balance for bank accounts, credit cards, or loans
Open the Transactions page.
Create an income transaction.
In the Description field, type 'Starting balance'.
Fill in the date, account name, and amount of the starting balance.
In the Category field, select an appropriate equity account for your business.
Select Save.
Enter a starting balance for non-payment accounts
Journal transactions can only be created in the web version of Wave.
Open the Transactions page.
Create a journal transaction.
In the Description field, type 'Starting balance'.
In the Date field, put in the starting balance date.
If the account is a liability account, enter the starting balance as a credit, and select the liability account you are entering the starting balance for. Enter a debit to your Owner's Equity account for the same amount.
If the account is an asset account, enter the starting balance as a debit, and select the asset account you are entering the starting balance for. Enter a credit to your Owner's Equity account for the same amount.
Select Save.
Starting balance transaction when you connect your bank or credit card
Automatic bank transaction imports are part of Wave’s Pro Plan. Learn more about Wave’s plans or how to subscribe.
When you connect your bank account or credit card for transaction imports, Wave enters the starting balance for you. These starting balance transactions have the description "Starting balance for".
chunks.category: Help Center > Accounting > Key accounting concepts

chunks.title: Starting balances: What they are, and how to enter them in Wave
chunks.content: If you enter transactions within the fiscal year with dates before this starting balance transaction, make sure you adjust the date and amount so it's the first transaction for the account.

chunks.title: Delete a bill
chunks.content:
On the left-side menu, click Purchases > Bills.
Find the bill you want to delete and click the arrow button to its right.
Click Delete from the drop-down menu.
Paid bills can’t be deleted. To remove the payment, select View/Edit from the drop-down menu, then click the trash can icon next to the payment.
Click Delete again in the pop-up to confirm.
Deleted bills can’t be recovered.

chunks.title: View or edit a bill
chunks.content:
On the left-side menu, click Purchases > Bills.
Click the arrow button to the right of the bill you want to view or edit.
Click View/Edit in the drop-down menu. 
View or edit sending details:
Vendor
Currency
Bill Date 
Due Date
P.O./S.O.
Bill #
Memo / Notes 
View or edit bill details:
Item(s) - click Add a line to add a new item.
Expense Category
Description
Quantity
Price

Click Save.

chunks.title: Add a payment to a bill
chunks.content:
To add a payment to a bill
On the left-side menu, click Purchases > Bills.
Click Record a payment to the right of the bill you want to add a payment to.
In the Record a manual payment pop-up, fill in the following details:
Payment method
Amount
Payment date
Payment account

chunks.title: Bookkeep a deposit or prepayment to a customer credit account
chunks.content:
Each customer you add to Wave will automatically have a Wave-made customer credit account to use for invoice deposits or prepayments.
If you previously used a manually created customer credit account and there is a balance, see Transfer a deposit or prepayment from a manually created customer credit account.
If you receive a customer deposit or prepayment and do not have an invoice to apply the funds to, bookkeep the funds to the customer’s credit account.
On the left side menu, click Accounting > Transactions.
Find the deposit transaction or create a new income transaction, and enter the date, amount and account.
For the Category, click Customer Prepayment, Deposit, or Payment on Account, then select the customer. This increases their prepayment account by the deposit amount.
To track your customer credits, view the customer credit report.
Learn how to apply a customer credit to an invoice.
chunks.category: Help Center > Accounting > Accounting for your sales

chunks.title: Import a customer list
chunks.content:
You can import your customer contacts into your Wave account using two methods: through your Wave account with a CSV file or through Wave’s Google Sheets integration, Wave Connect.
Import a CSV file
Import using Wave Connect
Import a CSV file
Step 1: Prepare your CSV file
Export your contacts from the platform where they're stored (e.g., Gmail, Outlook, Apple Contacts) into a CSV file.
Download then open this sample CSV file to see how you should organize your file for it to import successfully into Wave.
Open your customer contacts file and compare it to the sample CSV template. Copy the appropriate columns from your spreadsheet into the Wave template. Ensure that each contact includes at least one of the following or the import will not work: Company name, First name, Last name.
After organizing the data, save your file.
Step 2: Import the CSV file into Wave
If you do not have any customers in Wave, add a customer first. Then, at the top right corner, you will see the Import from CSV button.
Log in at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Sales & Payments > Customers.
Click Import from CSV.
Click Choose File, locate the CSV file you've prepared, and then click Upload and preview customers.
Review your data: Check that the customer information is correctly aligned with the proper headers (e.g., company names in the Company Name column, email addresses in the Email column).
Once you proceed, you won’t be able to undo the import. You can edit customer information later, but only one contact at a time.
Click Yes, proceed with import to finish the process.
Import using Wave Connect
Step 1: Set up Wave Connect
Download and install Wave Connect.
In Google Sheets, click Extensions > Wave Connect > Upload Customers. The Wave Connect add-on will appear on the right side of your sheet.
Under Step 1: Prepare Input Sheet, click the Prepare Input Sheet button to generate the customer upload template.
Step 2: Enter customer data

chunks.title: Import a customer list
chunks.content:
Enter your customers' data in each row of the template. Only the Customer Name field is required.
Choose country and province format: You can select whether to enter the country and province or state by name, or by the 2-letter ISO code.
Step 3: Validate and upload data
After entering the data, click Step 2: Validate Data and then click Validate Data.
If Wave Connect detects any issues it will alert you in Step 2 and under column R of the input sheet. Correct the data and click Validate Again.
When validation is successful, click Continue.
Review your customer information to ensure everything is correct.
Under Step 3: Upload Data, click Upload Customers.
If you have multiple business profiles, a pop-up will ask you to confirm the business profile for the import. To select a different business, click Cancel and select the correct business from the drop-down menu on the right side of the sheet.
Once you're ready, click Ok to start the import.
If you leave the currency column blank, Wave automatically applies your default business currency to the customer’s invoices.

chunks.title: Taxes: Recoverable vs. Non-Recoverable
chunks.content:
What is recoverable tax?
What is non-recoverable tax?
What is recoverable tax?
A tax is recoverable if you can deduct the tax you paid to other businesses from the tax you collect from your customers.
If you buy something for your business, you pay tax on your purchase. You can deduct this tax from the tax you collect from your customers.
For example, if you pay $1 in tax on a purchase for your business, and collect $5 in tax from your own sales, you would owe the government $4.
What is non-recoverable tax?
A tax is non-recoverable if you must remit the full amount you've collected from customers, regardless of what you may have paid.
If you buy something for your business, you pay tax on your purchase. This tax cannot be deducted from the tax you collect from your customers.
For example, if you pay $1 in tax on a purchase for your business, and collect $5 in tax from your own sales, you would owe the government the full $5.
Once you create a tax, you cannot change the recoverable or non-recoverable option. Learn how to Add, edit or delete a sales tax.

chunks.title: View and understand your sales tax report
chunks.content:
The sales tax report is only available on the web version of Wave.
The sales tax report records the sales taxes you have collected, which provides insight into what your business owes to the government.
View the sales tax report
Understand the sales tax report
Export a statement
View the sales tax report
On the left-side menu, click Reports, then Sales Tax Report.
Select your date range or input a custom date range.
Select the Report Type from Accrual (Paid and Unpaid) or Cash Basis (Paid).
Accrual (Paid and Unpaid) includes income and expenses. Non-cash expenses like depreciation and amortization are included.
Cash Basis (Paid) includes income that has been invoiced but not yet received and expenses that have been billed but not yet paid.
Click Update Report to review your statement.
If you’re unsure about which basis to use or if it’s your first time filing, consult with your bookkeeper or accountant.
Understand the sales tax report
Sales & Purchases
The top section of the report summarizes the total amount of each sales tax set up in your account from collected tax on sales and paid tax on purchases:
Tax: Name and percentage of each sales tax
Sales Subject to Tax: Total sales to which the tax was applied
Tax Amount on Sales: Total amount of tax collected on those sales
Purchases Subject to Tax: Total purchases to which the tax was applied
Tax Amount on Purchases: Total amount of tax paid (only shown if the tax is set up as a recoverable tax)
Net Tax Owing: Net amount of tax due to or from your tax authority for the reporting period
The tax amounts on sales and purchases may not match the debits and credits in the account transactions report as it shows the net amount. Sales tax in Wave is calculated per item and rounded to the nearest two decimal places.
Payments & Balances Owing
The bottom section summarizes payments and refunds related to each sales tax for the selected period:
Starting Balance: Amount due to or from the tax authority at the beginning of the reporting period

chunks.title: View and understand your sales tax report
chunks.content:
Net Tax Owing: Comes from the last column of the Sales & Purchases section; it shows the net amount due to or from the tax authority
Less Payments to Government: Shows any payments made and any refunds received for each sales tax
Ending Balance: Totals all columns, resulting in a net amount due or receivable for each sales tax. This final balance matches the ending balance of the tax account on your balance sheet.
For more insights into Wave's reporting features, check out the Video: Wave’s Reports Tour.
Export a statement
To export your sales tax report, at the top right corner, click Export, then select CSV or PDF format. The statement will download to your browser.

chunks.title: Change your fiscal year-end
chunks.content:
Wave sets your fiscal year-end to December 31st by default. To change this date:
Log in to your Wave account at waveapps.com.
At the top right corner, click your business name, then Business settings.
On the Settings menu, under Accounting, click Dates & Currency.
Choose the month and day of your business fiscal year-end.
Click Save.
Wave uses the Year-Month-Day format for dates which cannot be customized.
chunks.category: Help Center > Manage Your Account > Business Settings

chunks.title: Depreciation in Wave
chunks.content:
When you record a purchase as a capital asset, rather than an expense, at the time of purchase, the expense of owning the item is spread over its expected useful life. This is depreciation.
For example, if you purchase a computer for $1,800 and expect to use it for 3 years, you would expense one-third of the cost as depreciation each year.
For more information on depreciation, or when to account for it, contact an accountant.
Create a depreciation account
Record depreciation
Create a depreciation account
Log in at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Accounting > Chart of Accounts.
At the top right corner, click Add a New Account.
For the Account Type, select Depreciation & Amortization.
Name the account something relevant to depreciation.
Click Save.
This account will be an offset to the value of the asset account. Wave automatically creates a Depreciation Expense account under Expenses in your chart of accounts.
Record depreciation
Log in at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Accounting > Transactions.
At the top right, click Add transaction > Add journal entry.
Enter a description and select the date.
In the Debit column, for the category, click Depreciation Expense, and enter the amount.
In the Credit column, for the category, click the depreciation account you created, and enter the same amount as the debit column.
Click Save.
chunks.category: Help Center > Accounting > Key accounting concepts

chunks.title: Track inventory in Wave
chunks.content:
Inventory is a stock of physical items your business has purchased to sell. Inventory is a business asset.
Wave does not calculate or track the unit value of inventory for your business. Tracking inventory in Wave is based on the monetary value you calculate for the units.
Create inventory accounts
Record the purchase of inventory
Record the sale of inventory
Create inventory accounts
You need two accounts for each type of inventory: an inventory asset account and a cost of goods sold expense account. The inventory asset account is for items that you have purchased with the intention of selling but have not yet sold. The cost of goods sold expense account is for items that you purchased and already sold.
Learn how to add a new account to your chart of accounts.
Record the purchase of inventory
Log in at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Accounting > Transactions.
Locate the inventory purchase transaction or create an expense transaction.
If you made a bulk purchase for multiple inventory types, split the transaction.
For the Category, select the inventory asset account you created for that inventory type.
Fill in any remaining details.
Record the sale of inventory
Log in at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Accounting > Transactions.
Locate the sale transaction or create an income transaction.
For the Category, if you have an invoice associated with the sale, select Payment received for an invoice in Wave, then select the outstanding invoice. If you do not have an invoice, select the appropriate income account.
When you record an inventory sale, you must also update the cost of goods sold account. To update this account:
Create a journal transaction. On the first line, select your cost of goods sold account. This debits the account.
Enter the actual cost of the inventory item, not how much the customer paid.
On the second line, select your inventory asset account, which represents your stock level. This credits the account.
Enter the same amount as on the first line.

chunks.title: Track inventory in Wave
chunks.content:
Click Save.
Use your balance sheet to check the balance of your accounts. Your profit & loss statement shows how your business performed after the sale.
If you sell a lot of the same inventory, you can update your cost of goods sold expense account in bulk at the end of a specific period. Create a journal transaction that accounts for all inventory sold during that period rather than after each sale.

chunks.title: Import transactions automatically by connecting a bank account
chunks.content:
Automatic bank transaction imports are part of Wave’s Pro Plan. Learn more about Wave’s plans or how to subscribe.
Connecting a bank account to auto-import transactions to your Transactions page also helps automate your bookkeeping in Wave. Learn more about automated bookkeeping with auto-updates.
Transactions generally update every 24 hours but can take up to 7 days depending on your bank. Learn more in Understand bank connections.
There is no limit to how many bank accounts you can connect to import transactions.
To connect your bank account:
Log in to your Wave account at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Banking > Connected Accounts.
If this is your first bank connection, jump to step 4. If you have existing bank connections, at the top right, click Connect account, or toggle your account ON.
Select from the banks presented or enter the name of your bank in the search bar.
In the pop-up window, click Continue, then follow the prompts to sign in to your online banking.
If you have multiple accounts under the same financial institution, all of the supported accounts will appear in Wave. Select the accounts you want to import transactions from. Learn more about the supported account types for bank connections.
Wave does not support selecting only specific accounts from an institution to appear in Wave. If you do not want to import transactions for a specific account, turn the toggle off for that account.
Select an account in your chart of accounts for each bank account you toggle imports on. To create a new account to import to, select New account.
Click Edit date to choose how far back to import your transactions. Depending on your bank, you may be able to import up to 18 months of transactions.
To import older transactions, download electronic statements from your bank and upload them to Wave, or use Wave’s Google Sheets integration, Wave Connect.
chunks.category: Help Center > Transaction Imports > Bank Connections

chunks.title: Import transactions automatically by connecting a bank account
chunks.content: You cannot rename or nickname bank accounts you connect in Wave. The default name is based on how Plaid fetches the information from your bank.
chunks.category: Help Center > Transaction Imports > Bank Connections

chunks.title: Delete your Wave account
chunks.content:
Deleting your Wave account cannot be undone. Be sure you have extracted all the information you require before closing your account. Learn how to export your data.
Deleting your Wave account deletes all your personal and business data for all businesses in your account. After your account is deleted, you can register again using the same email address.
If you have any payroll subscriptions, you must cancel them before deleting your account.
To delete your account:
Ensure you're in the account you want to delete by checking the business name in the top right corner.
Click your business name. From the drop-down menu, click Profile settings.
Click Personal Information on the left.
Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Close This Wave Account.
Select a reason for leaving from the drop-down menu.
Confirm you want to continue by clicking Permanently Close All My Businesses in Wave. You can cancel your request by clicking Cancel.
You will receive an email at your primary email address. To permanently delete your account, click the link in the email to confirm.
chunks.category: Help Center > Manage Your Account > Manage Your Profile

chunks.title: What is a payment account?
chunks.content:
A payment account is any account that you use to deposit funds or to spend money. This may include bank accounts, credit cards, or lines of credit.
You can create payment accounts in your Chart of Accounts. Learn how to add a new account or category. If you connect your bank for transaction imports, you can choose a payment account to import to or import to a new account in your Chart of Accounts.
Automatic bank transaction imports are part of Wave’s Pro Plan. Learn more about Wave’s plans or how to subscribe.
chunks.category: Help Center > Accounting > Chart of accounts

chunks.title: Change the owner email address of your Wave account
chunks.content:
To change the owner or primary email address of your Wave account, you must first add a new email to replace the current one.
An email address can only be associated with one Wave account.
Log in to your Wave account at waveapps.com.
At the top right corner, click your business name, then Profile settings.
In the Settings menu, click Emails. If you log in using Google and do not have a password set up, click on Password & Security first, then create a password to enable the Emails tab.
Click Add new email.
Enter the new email address, then click Add email address.
Wave will send a verification email to the new address. Check your inbox and click the verification link in the email.
To set the new email address as the primary email:
Return to the Emails page.
Click the star icon next to the new email address.
Click the trash can icon next to the old email address, then click Delete email.
chunks.category: Help Center > Manage Your Account > Manage Your Profile

chunks.title: Add a new business to your Wave account
chunks.content:
Wave allows you to maintain up to 15 business profiles within one Wave account. Wave is only available for businesses in Canada and the United States. US territories are not supported.
To add a new business:
Log in to your account at waveapps.com.
Click your business name in the top right corner.
Click Switch businesses then Create new business.
If you have multiple businesses in your account, scroll down to see this button.
Fill in the fields under Create a business;
Enter your company name.
Select a business type and organizational type.
Fill in your country and business currency.
Click Next, select plan to choose between Wave’s Starter and Pro Plans.
Your new business will appear in the drop-down menu in the top right of your screen, along with your other businesses and Personal tabs. 
If you have reached Wave’s maximum business profile limit, you will not be able to add a new business. To create space for a new business profile, you can create a new Wave account, by following the steps in How to Move Your Data Between Wave Accounts or From Another Accounting System.
There is no limit to the number of businesses you can be added to as a collaborator.
Learn how to switch between businesses in Switch between business profiles or Wave accounts.
chunks.category: Help Center > Manage Your Account > Manage Your Profile

chunks.title: Edit a customer
chunks.content:
Edit a customer in your web browser
Edit a customer in the Wave mobile app
Edit a customer in your web browser
Log in to your account at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Sales & Payments > Customers.
Find the name of the customer whose information you would like to edit, then click on their name to view their profile.
Click Edit customer at the top right.
If you change a customer’s email and they receive recurring invoices, you also need to update their email on the recurring invoice.
Make the required changes, then click Save.
  Edit a customer in the Wave mobile app
Log in to the Wave mobile app.
Tap Sales on the bottom menu, then tap Customers in the submenu.
Tap on the name of the customer, then make the required changes.
If you change a customer’s email and they receive recurring invoices, you also need to update their email on the recurring invoice.
Tap Save.

chunks.title: Edit your business information
chunks.content:
Editing your business information in your profile settings changes what your customer sees on past and future invoices.
The contact information on file for your online payments or payroll account isn’t updated when you change your business information in your profile settings.
If your business information for payroll has changed, follow the steps in Edit your payroll business information.
If your business information for online payments has changed, open Mave, Wave’s automated chatbot, and type change info in payment account. Mave will help collect any relevant details and direct you to the appropriate support. Learn how to open Mave in Get support with Wave.
Edit your business information in a web browser
Edit your business information in the Wave mobile app
Edit your business information in a web browser
In the top right corner, click your business name, then Profile settings.
In the Profile menu, click on Businesses.
Click the pencil icon to the right of the business you want to edit the details of.
Edit any details, then click Save.
Edit your business information in the Wave mobile app
On the bottom menu, tap Dashboard, then tap More in the top right corner.
Tap Edit business info below your business name.
To edit your business name, address, and contact details, tap each field then make your changes.
To save edits to your business name, tap Save. To save edits to your business’s address or contact details, tap Done.
Tap Save.
chunks.category: Help Center > Manage Your Account > Manage Your Profile

chunks.title: I can't change my business type
chunks.content:
Choosing a business type one-time decision when you create a Wave business. Wave uses this information during the setup process only to determine which income and expense accounts to create. Once your account is created, the business type can't be changed, but it doesn't impact what actions you can take in Wave.
If you want to change your business type to update your list of income and expense accounts, you can add or delete accounts at any time instead.
If your business structure has changed, follow the steps in What to do when your business structure changes.
chunks.category: Help Center > Manage Your Account > Troubleshooting Problems in Wave

chunks.title: Adding a user who is already a Wave customer
chunks.content:
This feature is part of Wave’s Pro Plan. Learn more about Wave’s plans or how to subscribe.
When you invite another Wave user to become a collaborator on your business, they will see both yours and their own business profiles in their list of businesses.
They can switch between businesses without having to log in and out of different Wave accounts.
To view a list of your businesses in your web browser, click your business name at the top-right. To view a list of your businesses in the Wave mobile app, open the Dashboard tab from the bottom menu, then, in the top left, tap your business name.
chunks.category: Help Center > Manage Your Account > Business Settings

chunks.title: Create a recurring invoice from a single invoice
chunks.content:
If you create a single invoice, then realize your customer will be making the same purchases on a recurring schedule, you can convert it to a recurring invoice. Recurring invoices are sent to your customer automatically on a set schedule.
To convert an invoice to a recurring invoice:
On the left-side menu, click Sales & Payments > Invoices.
Select the invoice.
At the top of the page, click More Actions, then Make Recurring.
Set up the recurring invoice.
When your invoice is scheduled to recur, Wave will automatically create it for you.
Some recurring invoice features may require your business to have Wave’s online payments feature or a subscription to Pro Plan.
chunks.category: Help Center > Invoices & Estimates > Recurring Invoices

chunks.title: The difference between creating and approving a draft invoice
chunks.content:
When you click Save and Continue to create a new invoice, Wave saves the invoice as a draft. Saving an invoice as a draft does not make any changes to your accounting or reports.
Approving a draft invoice allows you to send it to your customer or record a payment. Once you approve the draft, it reflects on your accrual basis reports. You cannot change approved invoices back into drafts.

chunks.title: Understand the chargeback process
chunks.content:
A chargeback occurs when a customer disputes a payment with their bank or credit card company and requests a refund for the payment.
When your customer initiates a chargeback with their credit card company, that company then notifies Wave.
Wave cannot assist with chargebacks on payments made using EFT or ACH bank transfers.
If you choose to dispute a chargeback, the entire process can take up to 90 days.
Day 1: Wave notifies you of a chargeback
When a chargeback is initiated, Wave sends you an email titled “[Action Required] - You have a disputed charge.” This email outlines the details of the chargeback and the next steps.
If your business is using the new online payment experience, you can also review the information within your Wave account. Learn how to review and respond to a chargeback.
Learn how to respond to a chargeback.
Day 2: Funds are withdrawn from your bank account
The full chargeback amount, plus a fee between $7 to $15, will be withdrawn from the bank account connected for payouts in Wave. The funds are held by the cardholder’s bank until the chargeback is dropped, accepted, or a decision is made by the bank about a dispute.
Day 10: Deadline to submit your dispute documents
You have 5 days from when the chargeback is initiated to submit your documentation to Wave to either fight the claim or prove that the customer dropped their chargeback.
If Wave doesn’t receive your documents in time, the chargeback can no longer be disputed.
For help preparing your dispute documents, see Put together your chargeback documents.
If your customer has dropped their chargeback, see What to do if your customer wants to drop a chargeback.
Days 10-80: Your document package is created and sent to your customer’s bank
After Wave receives your documents, our dispute team puts together a document package and sends it to your customer’s bank. Wave will notify you by email when this package has been sent.

chunks.title: Understand the chargeback process
chunks.content:
Your customer’s bank has up to 60 days from the date of document submission to review the information. The bank makes a final decision regarding whether or not the cardholder’s chargeback is legitimate. It’s common for banks to take the full 60 days to respond to a dispute claim. Wave will provide an update via email as soon as the banks have reached their decision on your claim.
Days 80-90: The cardholder’s bank decides the outcome
Wave will provide an update via email as soon as the banks have reached their decision on your claim.
If your business is using the new online payment experience, you can also view the decision on the chargeback payment in your Wave account on the Payments page.
If your customer drops their dispute, it can still take up to 60 days for your customer’s bank to close the case and return the disputed funds.
If the bank rules in your favor, your customer’s bank reimburses Wave for the chargeback. Wave will redeposit the withdrawn funds into your bank account, less the dispute fee. It can take up to 2 business days for you to receive the funds.
If the bank rules in your customer’s favor, Wave will notify you of the bank’s decision and any reasoning the bank has provided. The funds will not be returned to you.
The final decision cannot be overturned, and a chargeback cannot be disputed twice.

chunks.title: What is a compound tax?
chunks.content:
A compound tax, or stacked tax, is calculated on top of a primary tax. 
A compound tax will be calculated when you add additional taxes to an item on top of the primary tax. This tax is added on top of your item cost once it has the primary tax already added, rather than calculated from the untaxed item amount. 
Here's an example of how compound tax is calculated. We're using an item that costs $100:
Item Price $100.00
GST (5%) $ 5.00
Subtotal $105.00
PST (10%) $ 10.50
Total $115.50
If this were not a compound tax, then the PST (10%) would only be $10.00. Since it is compound, it is added on top of the already primary taxed amount, and so is $10.50 instead.

chunks.title: [US] Frequently asked questions about contractor Form 1099-NEC
chunks.content:
What is Form 1099-NEC?
Form 1099-NEC is a non-employee compensation (NEC) form given to contractors who have provided services for your business.
Will my contractors receive a Form 1099-NEC?
The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) requires Form 1099-NEC to be provided to contractors you have paid at least $600 during 2025.
If the following four conditions are met, you must typically report a payment as NEC:
The payments are to someone who is not an employee
The payments are for services within your trade or business operations (including government agencies and nonprofit organizations)
The payments are to an individual, partnership, estate, or, in some cases, a corporation
A minimum of $600 is paid to the payee during the tax year
Do I need to file my contractor’s Form 1099-NEC?
If you have an active payroll subscription that was fully set up prior to 2026, and all eligible bills were marked as paid in 2025, Wave files the federal Form 1099-NEC for each eligible contractor on your behalf, as well as mandated state and local filings. This means you do not need to file your Form 1099-NECs. You must provide a physical copy of their 1099-NEC to your eligible contractors by January 31.
Why can’t I see Form 1099-NEC in my Wave account?
You must have an active subscription to Wave’s payroll feature to access your forms.
Form 1099-NEC for eligible contractors will be available in Wave in the final week of January. You cannot view these forms before that week. Learn how to review and download your forms.
If it’s the last week of January and you do not see the forms in your Wave account, your contractor may not be eligible to receive a Form 1099-NEC.
I don’t want Wave to file my Form 1099-NEC. How can I file Form 1099-NEC myself?
If you have an active payroll subscription, Wave will file all eligible Form 1099-NEC’s on your behalf. You cannot opt out of this filing. If you file outside of Wave, the IRS may count the income twice for your eligible contractors.

chunks.title: [US] Frequently asked questions about contractor Form 1099-NEC
chunks.content:
If you do not have an active payroll subscription, you must generate and file federal Form 1099-NEC, as well as state/local filings, outside of Wave. To file Form 1099-NEC electronically with the IRS, use their FIRE (Filing Information Returns Electronically) or IRIS (Information Returns Intake System).
To file on paper, review the Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC. The IRS requires you to e-file if you have to submit more than 10 Form 1099-NEC. When you file on paper, you are required to submit a Form 1096 outside of Wave. This form is not sent to contractors and is not required if filing electronically.

5. Date range: View all transactions within a specific timeframe.
6. Wave auto-updates: View all transactions that have been automatically categorized or merged, or created from a scanned receipt.
7. Last modified date: View all transactions modified within a specific timeframe.
To sort your transactions, click Sort above the transaction list. You can sort from newest to oldest or oldest to newest based on the transaction date.
You can search for transactions by their description or amount. Enter the keywords or amount into the Search bar at the top right of the transactions list, then click the magnifying glass icon.
Filter and sort transactions in the mobile app

To filter transactions, tap Filter at the top left. There are 2 filter options:

chunks.title: Filter and sort your transactions

1. All receipts scanned: View all transactions created from scanned receipts.
2. Receipts scanned with missing info: View transactions created from a receipt scan that have missing details.
To sort your transactions, tap Sort at the top left. Tap the arrow on the right to switch from newest to oldest or oldest to newest based on the transaction date.

chunks.title: What to do if your customer wants to drop a chargeback
chunks.content:
If your customer wants to drop their chargeback claim, they must call their credit card company to drop the dispute. They should ask their credit card company for a Letter of Affirmation to confirm the dispute has been dropped, then provide you with a copy.
If a Letter of Affirmation is not available, you can provide a written letter stating that the dispute has been dropped. The letter must be signed by the cardholder and include their photo ID.
If a letter of affirmation is not available, provide a written letter signed by the cardholder stating the dispute has been dropped, and include their photo ID.
Once received, respond to your chargeback notification email from Wave with either the Letter of Affirmation or a signed written letter with the customer ID. These documents will be submitted in your document package to be reviewed by our payment processor and your customer’s bank to verify that the dispute can be closed.
The process can take up to 90 days to resolve.
Learn more in Understand the chargeback process.
If you have questions about a chargeback, our Support Team can help. To reach them, open Mave, Wave’s automated chatbot, and request a Support Agent.

chunks.title: Frequently asked questions about invoice and estimate attachments
chunks.content:
Invoice and estimate attachments are part of Wave’s Pro Plan. Learn more about Wave’s plans or how to subscribe.
  Why aren't my attachments appearing in the email sent to my customer?
If you upload files to an invoice or estimate exceeding 5MB, they will not appear as attachments in the email when you send them. However, the attachments will be visible at the bottom when the customer views the invoice or estimate. 
If the total file size is below 5MB, make sure to check the box to show the attachments in the email when you send an invoice or estimate.
Where do my attachments go if they're not in the email?
The attachments are always visible at the bottom of an invoice or estimate when viewing it.
How will my customer know that attachments are associated with an invoice or estimate if they're not included in the email?
On the email your customer receives, they will see a View attachments button along with the View invoice or View estimate button. Clicking View attachments in the email will take them directly to the attachments section of the invoice or estimate.
What file types are supported for invoice and estimate attachments?
JPG, PNG, GIF, PDF, DOC/DOCX, XLS/XLSX, and CSV file types are supported.
Are there any limits to the number or size of files I can upload?
You can upload a maximum of 25 files and up to 20MB in total. You can upload up to 10 files at a time.

chunks.title: Use two-factor authentication (2FA) to log in to Wave
chunks.content:
Two-factor authentication, or 2FA, is an additional layer of security for your Wave account. 2FA helps verify your identity during login and prevents unauthorized access to your information.
When 2FA is turned on, you are prompted to enter a one-time verification code each time you sign in to your Wave account. You can choose to receive this code by text to your mobile number or through an authenticator app. This verifies that it is you logging in.
Never share this verification code with others.
Turn on two-factor authentication in your web browser
Turn on two-factor authentication in the Wave mobile app
Download an authenticator app
Frequently asked questions
Turn on two-factor authentication in your web browser
At the top right corner, click your business name, then click Profile Settings.
In the Profile menu, click Password & Security.
To switch authenticator methods, next to your active method, click Turn off, then click Turn off… to confirm.
Click Set up authenticator app or Set up phone number.
If using an app, scan the QR code using the third-party authentication app. If using your phone number, enter your number.
Click Continue.
Enter the six-digit verification code you received, via text message or from your authenticator app, into Wave and click Continue.
Wave creates your recovery keys, then lists them in the next pop-up window. To save your keys, click Download (.txt file).
You can use a recovery key to log in to your Wave account if you're having trouble receiving a verification code. Each key can only be used once. Never share any of these keys with others.
Click Done.
You will receive a confirmation email, and see an Active label under your chosen 2FA sign-in method.
If you’re having trouble setting up or using 2FA, contact support.
Turn on two-factor authentication in the Wave mobile app
Currently, you can only set up 2FA through the mobile app if your account location is Canada.
In the top-right corner, tap More.
Tap the General tab.
chunks.category: Help Center > Manage Your Account > Manage Your Profile

chunks.title: Use two-factor authentication (2FA) to log in to Wave

Tap Continue.
Enter the six-digit verification code you received, via text message or from your authenticator app, into Wave and tap Continue.
Wave creates your recovery keys, then lists them in the next pop-up window. To save your keys, tap Download (.txt file).
You can use a recovery key to log in to your Wave account if you're having trouble receiving a verification code. Each key can only be used once. Never share any of these keys with others.
Tap Done.
You will receive a confirmation email, and see an On label next to Two-factor authentication.
If you’re having trouble setting up or using 2FA, contact support.
Download an authenticator app
Authenticator apps generate a one-time verification code that you can use in addition to a password.
If you don’t have an authenticator app, popular choices include Google Authenticator and Microsoft Authenticator. Both can be downloaded from your phone's App Store.
Google Authenticator

For iOS, visit the Apple App Store.
For help setting up Google Authenticator on your device, see Google Account Help: Get verification codes with Google Authenticator.
Desktop browser authenticator

Microsoft Authenticator

For Android, visit the Google Play Store
For iOS, visit the Apple App Store
For help with app setup on your device, see Microsoft Support: How to add your accounts to Microsoft Authenticator.
Frequently asked questions

chunks.title: Use two-factor authentication (2FA) to log in to Wave
chunks.content:
For help troubleshooting Microsoft Authenticator, see Microsoft Support: Troubleshoot problems with Microsoft Authenticator.

For help troubleshooting Google Authenticator, see Google Account Help: Fix common issues with 2-Step Verification.
What if multiple people share the same login for my Wave account?
2FA codes can only be sent to one device, using one method, at a time.
To protect your account’s security, Wave does not recommend that multiple people use the same login credentials.
If multiple people need access to your Wave account, you can add them as collaborators. This allows them to use their own Wave account and login credentials to access your account.
Do collaborators need to set up 2FA?
Collaborators on accounts you own don’t need to activate 2FA to access your business, unless they have payroll management access.
They can set up 2FA on their own devices if they choose.
Where is the code I need to sign in?
You can find the code in the authenticator app you downloaded or in a text you received. To update your phone number, follow the steps in Update your phone number for two-factor authentication (2FA).
