chunks.title: View and understand your balance sheet
chunks.content:
The balance sheet is only available on the web version of Wave.
A balance sheet provides an overview of your business's assets, liabilities, and equity, to provide a tool for assessing your company's worth at a specific moment in time.
View the balance sheet
Understand the balance sheet
Export a statement
View the balance sheet
On the left-side menu, click Reports, then Balance Sheet.
Select your statement date.
Select the Report Type from Accrual (Paid and Unpaid) or Cash Basis (Paid).
Accrual (Paid and Unpaid) includes income and expenses. Non-cash expenses like depreciation and amortization are included.
Cash Basis (Paid) includes income that has been invoiced but not yet received and expenses that have been billed but not yet paid.
Click Update Report to review your statement.
An overview of your cash and bank balance, income to be received, and the expenses to be paid for your selected date is displayed at the top of your report.
You can view your statement in full in either the Summary or Details tab:
The Summary tab provides an overview of your total balance for asset, liability, and equity accounts.
The Details tab provides an in-depth look at the specific accounts and balances within your business asset, liability, and equity categories.
Understand the balance sheet
The core accounting equation is: Assets = Liabilities + Equity.
This equation shows that what a business owns (assets) is funded through borrowing (liabilities) or owner contributions and profits (equity).
Assets
The first section lists all assets owned by the company. This includes your Cash and Bank, Other Current Assets, and Long-term Assets. Assets are organized from the most liquid, or most easily converted to cash, to the least liquid.
Liabilities
The second section lists all current and long-term liabilities. Liabilities are in order of shortest term to longest term.
Equity

chunks.title: View and understand your balance sheet
chunks.content:
The final section details the equity of the business. Depending on the business structure, this may include owner or partner equity, owner investment and draws, common stock, retained earnings, and additional paid-in capital.
For more information on Wave’s reporting features, watch the Video: Wave’s Reports Tour.
Export a statement
To export your balance sheet, at the top right corner, click Export, then select CSV or PDF format. The statement will download to your browser.

chunks.title: View and understand your cash flow statement
chunks.content:
The cash flow statement is only available on the web version of Wave.
The cash flow statement tracks the movement of money within your business for a specific period, which provides a look at the sources and use of finances.
View the cash flow statement
Understand the cash flow statement
Export a statement
View the cash flow statement
An overview of your cash flow statement is available on your business dashboard. Learn more in Get insight into your business with the dashboard.
On the left-side menu, click Reports, then Cash Flow Statement.
Select your date range or input a custom date range.
To compare your statement with another time period, click Compare to a prior period and select the date range.
You can only view your cash flow statement on a cash basis.
Click Update Report.
An overview of your gross cash inflow, gross cash outflow, and net cash change for your selected timeframe is displayed at the top of your report. If you’re comparing report periods, the overall net cash change for each period, along with the difference between the two periods, is displayed.
You can view your statement in full in either the Summary or Details tab:
The Summary tab provides an overview of your business operating, investing, and financing activities, as well as the starting and ending balances.
The Details tab provides an in-depth look at the specific income and expense accounts that contribute to the inflow and outflow of money.
Understand the cash flow statement
All monetary transactions from physical cash, bank accounts, and unreconciled items like deposits and checks, are accounted for in the cash flow statement. They are categorized into three sections:
Operating Activities show the cash transactions related to regular business operations. This includes sales, purchases, inventory, payroll, sales taxes, and other related activities.
Investing Activities show the cash spent and received on fixed assets and long-term receivables. This includes property, plant and equipment, and loans.

chunks.title: View and understand your cash flow statement
chunks.content:
Depreciation is not considered an investing activity as it’s a non-cash expense.
Financing Activities show the cash inflows and outflows made by the business owner. This includes owner investments and loan proceeds, dividends and draws, and principal loan payments.
The cash flow statement is the only report that shows the owner’s investments and drawings from the business.
At the bottom of the report, there is an Overview where the net total from these three sections is combined with the business starting balance to determine the ending cash balance.
For more information on Wave’s reporting features, check out the Video: Wave’s Reports Tour.
Export a statement
To export your profit & loss statement, at the top right corner, click Export, then select CSV or PDF format. The statement will download to your browser.

chunks.title: Accrual vs. cash-basis reporting
chunks.content:
Wave offers both accrual and cash basis accounting options for reporting. By default, all reports in Wave are set to accrual accounting.
If you're unsure whether accrual or cash basis reporting is best for your business, consult with an accountant for guidance.
Accrual accounting
Cash basis accounting
Switch between accrual and cash basis accounting
Accrual accounting
Accrual accounting records all transactions, including those that are due but have not yet been paid.
This includes:
Accounts receivable, or income owed to you
Accounts payable, or expenses you owe
Cash basis accounting
Cash basis accounting only records income and expense transactions when funds have been received or paid.
This includes:
Cash transactions
Credit card transactions
Short-term and long-term assets (e.g., employee receivables, capitalized equipment)
Short-term and long-term liabilities (e.g., sales tax payable, loans)
Credit card transactions are considered cash expenditures for tax purposes. This means you deduct the expense when you charge the purchase, not when you pay off the card balance. The other assets and liabilities reflect activity based on cash transactions, even if there is no immediate impact on the income statement.
Switch between accrual and cash basis reporting
Cash basis reporting is available on the profit & loss statement, balance sheet, sales tax report, trial balance, cash flow, and account transactions report.
Accrual basis reporting is not available on the cash flow report.
  To switch between accrual and cash basis accounting in Wave:
On the left-side menu, click Reports.
Open your chosen report.
At the top of the report, under Report Type, click the dropdown arrow and select Accrual or Cash Basis.
Click the question mark icon beside Report Types for more information about the two types of accounting.
Learn more about Wave’s reporting features in Video: Wave’s Reports Tour.

chunks.title: View and understand your profit & loss statement
chunks.content:
The profit & loss statement is only available on the web version of Wave.
The profit & loss statement, or income statement, shows the money earned and spent over a specific period, providing a look into business profitability.
View your profit & loss statement
Understand the profit & loss statement
View your profit & loss statement
An overview of your profit & loss report is available on your business dashboard. Learn more in Get insight into your business with the dashboard.
On the left-side menu, click Reports.
Click Profit & Loss (Income Statement).
Select a standard date range from the drop-down, or a custom date range.
To compare your statement with another time period, click Compare to a prior period and select a date range.
Set the Report Type as Accrual (Paid and Unpaid) or Cash Basis (Paid).
Accrual includes income, cash expenses, and non-cash expenses like depreciation and amortization.
Cash Basis includes income that has been invoiced but not yet received and expenses that have been billed but not yet paid.
Click Update Report to generate your report.
You can view a summarised or detailed breakdown of your statement:
The Summary tab contains an overview of your income, cost of goods sold and gross profit, as well as your operating expenses and net profit.
The Details tab lists the specific income and expense account balances that contribute to the business's gross and net profits.
Understand your profit & loss statement
At the top of a single period report is an overview of your income, expenses and net profit for the date range.
If you’re comparing report periods, you'll see the net profit for each period and the difference in profits instead. You'll also see the dollar amount and percentage change between periods. An arrow indicates whether each amount has increased or decreased.
Income and gross profit
The first section of your profit & loss statement details the income accounts and the cost of goods sold (COGS) accounts that make up your business's gross profit.

chunks.title: View and understand your profit & loss statement
chunks.content:
Gross profit is the total revenue minus the COGS. The COGS includes the costs to produce your product or service. To determine your gross profit margin, the percentage of revenue kept after covering your COGS, divide your gross profit by your total revenue, then multiply by 100.
Operating expenses and net profit
The other section of your profit & loss statement details the operating expense accounts that are subtracted from your gross profit to calculate the business’s overall net profit. Operating expenses are not directly related to product or service production. Examples of these expenses are payroll and wages, advertising, and insurance.
Net profit is your business’s overall profitability. If the total is negative, this is a net loss. Use this number to track your business growth, changes in sales volume and changes in expenses.
For more information on Wave’s reporting features, check out the Video: Wave’s Reports Tour.

chunks.title: Record gift certificates
chunks.content:
Gift certificates represent money that customers have paid to you in advance to receive products or services later.

chunks.title: Using business policies and Terms of Services in Wave
chunks.content:
As your policies and Terms of Services should be specific to your business, consult with a legal professional to build them.
You can add policies and Terms of Services to the Notes/Footer section of invoices or estimates, or add them as an attachment.
Refund policy
Shipping policy
Terms of Service
Refund policy
A refund policy helps to protect both you and your customers in the event of a return or unforeseen circumstance. This policy provides your customers with your business’s specific policies and procedures for refunds, exchanges, and cancellations.
You can choose to require acknowledgement of your policy before receiving a credit card payment, which can help protect you in payment disputes.
Shipping policy
A shipping policy provides your customers with important information about your business’s shipping practices. It should be accessible to customers prior to them making a purchase and contain information related to shipping costs and timelines.
A shipping policy can include:
The methods of shipping available
Where you ship to
How long shipping takes
Shipping restrictions
What to do if a package arrives damaged
Terms of Service
A Terms of Service agreement protects your business.
If a customer isn’t happy with your service or is in financial distress, they may choose to dispute their credit card payment instead of asking for a refund.
In many cases, simple terms of service can give you the documentation you need if your customer disputes a payment.
A Terms of Service can outline:
What your customer is receiving and when they should expect to receive it
Your refund policy
Your cancellation policy
Your shipping policy
A force majeure clause to protect against unforeseen circumstances outside of your business’ control
A limitation of liability to protect against damages that may be caused as a result of your work
A no guarantee clause to confirm that your product or service does not promise a specific outcome
Learn how to add a payments Terms of Service on an invoice.

chunks.title: How to account for donations
chunks.content:
In addition to your business' usual income and expenses, you might also give or receive monetary donations. This article explains how to record both the giving and receiving of monetary donations & gifts.
To record the acceptance of a donation:
Open the Transactions page.
Locate your bank-imported income transaction or add an income transaction.
If you add a new transaction:
For the Account, select the bank account these funds were deposited into.
For the Amount, enter the total donation amount.
Open the category field and create a new income account to categorize the transaction to.
Select Save.
To record the giving of a donation:
Open the Transactions page.
Locate your bank-imported expense transaction or add an expense transaction.
If you add a new transaction:
For the Account, select the bank account these funds were withdrawn from.
For the Amount, enter the total amount donated.
Open the category field and create a new expense account, under the Account Type Operating Expense, to categorize the transaction to.
Select Save.
What's next?
In terms of recording the donation acceptance/giving, you're all set! If you're wondering how these items affect your business' bottom line, you can see this in Reports > Profit & Loss, where all income and expenses are included, regardless of type. 
The Reports page is only available in the web browser version of Wave.
If you're curious about how this impacts your tax filings, this varies region to region. It will be best to consult with an accountant, as they'll be best equipped to inform you about how charitable donations are taxed, not taxed, or otherwise need to be recorded in your specific region.

chunks.title: Add a discount to an invoice
chunks.content:
The first time you approve an invoice with a discount, Wave creates an account called Sales Discounts. This account is under the Income tab in your Chart of Accounts.
Once an invoice is approved, the discounted amount is recorded under Sales Discounts.
Discounts appear as negative amounts on your Profit & Loss Report because they reduce your income.
Each invoice can have only one discount.
Add a discount to an invoice in your web browser
Add a discount to an invoice in the Wave mobile app
Add a discount to an invoice in your web browser
On the left-side menu, click Sales & Payments > Invoices.
Select the invoice, then click Edit Invoice.
Below the subtotal, click Add a discount. A line labelled Discount will appear.
From the dropdown menu, select $ to discount a dollar amount or % to discount a percentage of the subtotal.
Enter the dollar amount or percentage to discount.
Discounts reduce the invoice total before tax is calculated.
Add a discount to an invoice in the mobile app
On the bottom menu, tap Sales > Invoices.
Tap the invoice, then tap the pencil icon.
Scroll down to the Amount due section, and tap Add discount.
Select to discount a fixed amount or a percentage of the subtotal.
Enter the dollar amount or percentage to discount.
Tap Done.
Discounts reduce the invoice total before tax is calculated.

chunks.title: View a customer's invoicing summary
chunks.content:
You can find customer summaries without having to jump between pages in Wave by using customer filters on the invoice list page. This can be helpful when you need one place to get a better idea of how your customers are doing.
To view a customer summary, navigate to Sales & Payments > Invoices and search for a customer using the customer filter. The customer summary will appear above the invoice list.
The customer summary contains:
Customer details: click the customer's name to reveal their phone number and email address, and the View profile link. Click this link to view their profile on the Customers page.
Total unpaid: the total amount that a customer owes you whether the amount is overdue or not
Overdue: the total amount that a customer owes you that is overdue
Paid last 12 months: the total amount a customer has paid you over the last 12 months
Last item sent: this indicates what kind of communication item was last sent to a customer and when it was sent. This includes invoices, invoice reminders, and customer statements. This will show items sent on and after July 14, 2020.
Customer action: if a customer has 2 or more open invoices, you will see the option to Send statement. This allows you to send a Customer Statement. If a customer has 1 invoice open, you will see the option to Send reminder. This allows you to send an Invoice Reminder. If your customer has no open invoices, no customer action will be suggested.

chunks.title: Why can’t I delete certain customers?
chunks.content:
There are a few possible reasons why you can’t delete a customer:
The customer is attached to an invoice or estimate
The customer has a balance in their customer credit account
You are trying to delete multiple customers at once
The customer is attached to an invoice or estimate
A customer cannot be deleted if they are attached to an invoice or estimate, as that may impact your bookkeeping.
If you have a duplicate customer profile and can’t delete it because it's associated with an invoice or estimate, follow the steps in Fix duplicate customer profiles.
The customer has a balance in their customer credit account
A customer cannot be deleted if there is a balance in their customer credit account. To clear the balance, refund the amount to your customer or apply it to another invoice.
To change the method used to handle the overpayment and refund the amount, see Bookkeep invoice overpayments. To apply the credit to another invoice, follow the steps in Bookkeep customer credits.
You are trying to delete multiple customers at once
Deleting customers in bulk is not possible. Customer profiles need to be deleted one at a time.

chunks.title: Write off a foreign currency invoice
chunks.content:
To complete the steps in this article, log in to your account from a web browser at waveapps.com.
If you create an invoice in a foreign currency and realize later that you need to write it off as uncollectible, the process is a little different than if the invoice is in your business currency. By following these steps, you won’t recognize any gain or loss on the foreign currency exchange while successfully zeroing out your Accounts Receivable balance.
If the invoice is in your business currency, see Write off an invoice.
Create bad debt accounts
Record a payment
Create a transaction
Create bad debt accounts
To successfully write off a foreign currency invoice, you will need a Bad Debt Clearing account, as well as a Bad Debt Expense account, both in your business currency.
To create a Bad Debt Clearing account:
On the left side menu, select Accounting > Chart of Accounts.

Record a payment

Click Save.
On the invoice details page, select Record a payment manually.
In the Payment method drop-down, choose the method of refund.
In the Payment account drop-down back, choose the Bad Debt Clearing account.
Change the exchange rate to the rate from the invoice found in Step 1.
The amount in your business currency will be the same as on the invoice, make a note of this.
Click Submit.
Create a transaction

chunks.title: Submit your chargeback documents
chunks.content:
Once you’ve collected the documents you’re submitting to dispute a chargeback, you’ll fill out a merchant cover letter and submit the documents to Wave. When the two actions are done, Wave’s dispute team will review your documentation and assemble your case. If there are any questions regarding your documents, you will receive an email with additional questions about your claim.
For help preparing your documents for upload, see Put together your chargeback documents.
To fill out your merchant cover letter and submit your documents:
Find the email from Wave titled “[Action Required] - You have a disputed charge”.

Return to the email titled “[Action Required] - You have a disputed charge”.
Click Step 2: Dispute this chargeback to upload the documents to support your claim. If a section is not relevant to your claim, you do not need to upload a document there. What documents are relevant to a claim depends on the reason for the chargeback. chunks.title: Common chargeback reason codes
chunks.content:
Your chargeback notification email contains the reason that your customer provided to their bank for the chargeback. To successfully dispute the claim, you must provide documents that prove the reason for the chargeback is false.
Common chargeback reason codes, and documents to help dispute them, include:
Cancelled payment, merchandise, or service
This means the cardholder claims they no longer wanted to participate in or receive an ongoing service or merchandise, but were still charged for them.
Your documents must demonstrate that the cardholder did not cancel their product or service before it was provided to them, and that the customer was aware of, and agreed to, your cancellation policy and procedures.
If a payment was cancelled, your documents must demonstrate that the cancellation policy was violated, or the cardholder continued to benefit from or use the product or service after cancellation.
Credit not processed
This is used when the cardholder claims they were promised a refund or credit, and it was not provided to them.
Your documents must demonstrate that a refund has been issued to the cardholder or that they are not entitled to a refund.
To help track funds, if you receive a payment through Wave, issue any refunds for that payment through Wave. To help prevent refunds from being disputed, issue refunds to the original method of tender. Learn how to Refund a customer payment.
Defective/Not as described
This is used when the cardholder received a product or service that differed from the purchase agreement, including quality discrepancies.
Your documents must demonstrate that the cardholder paid for and received exactly what they expected.
Duplicate payment
This is used when the cardholder claims that they have been charged twice for the same service or product.

chunks.title: Common chargeback reason codes
chunks.content:
Your documents must demonstrate that the cardholder was charged the correct amount and that they were aware of the charge. Include the invoice or receipt of the payment that is claimed to be a duplicate, and explain why each payment is valid.
Fraud/No cardholder authorization
This is used when the cardholder does not recognize the charge or if their card has been compromised.
Your documents must demonstrate that the cardholder authorized the transaction and was aware of the charge. You may include proof of prior transactions with your business to support claims of this type.
Incorrect amount/Point of interaction error
This is used when a cardholder claims that an incorrect amount was charged to them.
TYour documents must demonstrate that the cardholder knew how much they would be charged and approved that amount. Provide proof that the amount charged was correct.
Merchandise/Services not received
This is used when the cardholder paid for a product or service and did not receive it.
Your documents must demonstrate that the cardholder is now in possession of the product or has received the service.

chunks.title: Foreign currency account balances in Wave
chunks.content:
Foreign currency account balances on reports
The balance of a foreign currency account on your balance sheet doesn’t always match what you might expect when you translate the foreign currency at the current exchange rate. The business currency balance in Wave is the sum of each transaction, so as rates change, the balance in your business currency changes too.
In your Account Transactions (General Ledger) report, a foreign currency account looks like this:
The balances of both currencies are the running totals of the starting balance plus or minus the individual transaction amounts. The exchange rate for each transaction depends on the source, which can mean a difference between the account balance in your reports and the current translated value.
When you reconcile a foreign currency account, the balance and transactions are in the foreign currency. When you enter the ending balance, it must also be in the foreign currency.
To adjust the balance of the foreign or business currency account so that the translated foreign currency balance matches the business currency balance, the account needs a revaluation. Our Support Team can help complete this. Open Mave, Wave’s automated chatbot, and type human support revaluation entry. Provide the name of the account and the date you need the account to be at zero.
For advice on your specific foreign currency transactions, consult your accountant or tax preparer.

chunks.title: Put together your chargeback documents
chunks.content:
When uploading your documents, the goal is to have your cardholder's bank quickly understand what they are looking at and how it supports your claim. Wave will supply the payment details and a copy of the invoice associated with the chargeback. If you have filled out the merchant cover letter from your chargeback email, Wave will also supply a cover letter with the file descriptions based on the information you submit.
Evidence limitations
Create a merchant statement of events
Add notes to your documentation
Keep information concise
Evidence limitations
Each file must be 1 MB or smaller, and all documents must not exceed a total of 8 MB.
For the best results, original documents should be in A4 or US Letter format
If submitting in JPG or TIFF format, all documents must not exceed a total of 10 MB
If submitting in PDF format, all documents must not exceed a total of 2 MB
You can submit up to 15 pages of information in a package. While your email outlines 20 pages, the additional 5 pages include the cover page and invoice information to be submitted by Wave.
Evidence is not accepted as a video file, audio file, zip file, or shareable outside links such as Google Drive, or Dropbox. All documents must be in English.
Create a merchant statement of events
This written statement tells the credit card company what the situation is and why the dispute should be ruled in your favor. Include a brief explanation of the services or merchandise that the cardholder purchased from you as well as a sequence of events. Be specific with dates and the work progress.
Add notes to your documentation
Add notes, arrows, boxes, circles, and other attention-drawing marks on your evidence. This helps provide additional context to the reviewing agent about what they are looking at and where to focus their attention. Do not label evidence as an Exhibit.
Block out sensitive information, such as full credit card numbers, and leave only the last 4 digits of the number visible.
Keep information concise

chunks.title: Put together your chargeback documents
chunks.content:
The dispute reason must be clear within the first 2-5 minutes of viewing your documentation package.
Include the most relevant information and documents to support your dispute claim. Determine which documents to provide in Documents to support your chargeback dispute.
Avoid jargon or evidence that someone outside your business will not understand.
When you have multiple images as evidence, you can place up to 6 on a single page. Use a text editor such as Microsoft Word, or Google Docs to place the images, then convert the document to a PDF file.

chunks.title: Customer Profiles
chunks.content:
A customer profile provides you with an overview of your customer's information, their invoice and payment history, and allows you to create and send invoices.
To access your customer’s profile:
On the left-side menu, click Sales & Payments > Customers.
Click on a customer's name to open their profile, or click the dropdown arrow to the far right to take action on their profile.
Click Edit customer at the top right to edit their profile.
Click More at the top right to create an invoice or estimate, send a statement, or delete your customer.
Within their profile, there are three different tabs:
Overview
Invoices
Activity
Overview tab
On the Overview tab, you can see all the important information surrounding your customer in a single view.
The Overview tab contains:
Contact details: primary contact details, secondary contact details, shipping address, and internal notes.
Invoice insights: the total unpaid amount, how much has been paid in the last 12 months and the last item that was sent, or marked as sent, to your customer.
Unpaid invoices: any invoices that have not yet been paid by your customer.
Saved cards: all of your customers' saved credit cards. 
Invoices tab
The Invoices tab shows all invoices associated with your customer. From this tab, you can create, approve and send invoices, record payments, and generate reminders.
To send invoices and reminders directly through Wave, subscribe to our Pro Plan. Learn more about subscribing to Pro Plan.
Activity tab
The Activity tab provides an overview of your history with your customer. Learn more in Customer Profile Activities.

chunks.title: Fix duplicate bank connections
chunks.content:
Automatic bank transaction imports are part of Wave’s Pro Plan. Learn more about Wave’s plans or how to subscribe.
Duplicate bank connections can occur if your bank account is connected more than once to import transactions. To fix duplicate bank connections, follow these steps in order of section.
Bank connections cannot be restored to a date or time in the past if a mistake is made. For assistance with handling duplicate bank connections, check out Wave Advisors. Learn more about Personalized help with Wave Advisors.
Turn off imports or delete duplicate accounts
If your connected bank account is used for online payments or payroll, Update your payout account or Update your payroll funding account before you delete the connection.
You can only delete duplicate bank connections if all accounts within the connection are duplicates. You can’t delete individual accounts, but you can toggle imports off to prevent duplicate transactions. To turn off imports or delete a connection:
Log in to your account at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Banking > Connected Accounts.
To turn off transaction imports, click the toggle next to Automatically import transactions into account.
To delete a duplicate bank connection, at the top right of the duplicate connection, click the trash can icon.
Update your chart of accounts
When a bank is connected for transaction imports, an account is automatically created in your chart of accounts to represent that bank account. When a duplicate connection is created, rename the duplicate account to avoid using it.
On the left-side menu, click Accounting > Chart of Accounts.
Locate the duplicate accounts.
To edit the duplicate account, to the right of the account, click the pencil icon.
Rename the account to something that will show it's a duplicate.
Click Save.
Review your transactions for duplicates
On the left-side menu, click Accounting > Transactions.
Click Filter, open the Category dropdown, and select the renamed duplicated account.
chunks.category: Help Center > Transaction Imports > Troubleshooting Tips

chunks.title: Fix duplicate bank connections
chunks.content:
Delete any duplicate transactions or move them to the correct account and merge them.
For help with bulk editing or deleting your transactions, see How to use bulk actions on transactions.
It is easy to make a mistake or delete the wrong transactions. For assistance with deleting transactions, check out Wave Advisors.
Archive duplicate accounts
Archiving an account in your chart of accounts will remove it from the drop-down menu on the Transactions page. To archive a duplicate account:
On the left-side menu, click Accounting > Chart of Accounts.
Click the pencil icon next to the duplicate account.
Select the checkbox next to Archive Account.
Click Save.

chunks.title: Frequently asked questions: Getting your books ready for Block Advisors or another tax preparer
chunks.content:
Frequently asked questions
How do I ensure my books are tax-ready?
To ensure your books are tax-ready, read our Accounting year-end checklist. Specific tax needs may vary by business and region. If you have specific questions about your tax filings, reach out to a tax professional.
How do I look for duplicates?
You can spot duplicates or discrepancies between your Wave account and your bank records by using the reconciliation tool. Learn how to Reconcile your books.
Why should I categorize my transactions?
Transactions imported into Wave typically include only a title, date, and amount. The benefits of categorization include:
It creates a clear paper trail of your business's financial activities.
It simplifies income declaration and expense write-offs when filing taxes.
It provides clarity for yourself, your accountant, or your tax preparer on the purpose of each transaction.
It enhances the resilience of your books in case of an audit.
Many reports in Wave depend on accurate categorization. By categorizing your transactions, you allow Wave to sort your data properly.
chunks.category: Help Center > Accounting > Key accounting concepts

chunks.title: [US] Tax filing with Block Advisors
chunks.content:
Wave allows US businesses to file taxes through Block Advisors, who are part of H&R Block. This integration lets you use your accounting data in Wave for tax filing.
The available filing options in your Wave account depend on your business structure, as this dictates the type of filing required by the IRS.
How do I contact Block Advisors?
For general inquiries, call H&R Block at 1-800-HR-BLOCK (472-5625).
If you're already working with a tax pro, log into your Block Advisors account to use secure messaging or schedule a phone appointment.
Why do I only have the option to file with a tax advisor?
If your business is structured as a multi-member LLC, S-Corp, or C-Corp, the required IRS filing is more complex than the Schedule C return used by sole proprietors and single-member LLCs. Wave allows you to connect with a tax pro to navigate these complexities.
If you selected the wrong business type when you first set up your business profile:
From the left-side menu, select the Perks page.
Scroll down to the More to explore section and select H&R Block. Wave will open the Tax Filing page in a new tab.
Scroll to the bottom of the Tax Filing page and click Tell us how your business is structured.
Select your business structure from the drop-down menu, then click Continue.
How much does it cost to use Block Advisors?
The cost depends on your business structure and the required IRS filing. For pricing details:
Log in at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, select Perks.
Scroll down to the More to explore section and select H&R Block. Wave will open the Tax Filing page with pricing information in a new tab.
This pricing information is the base cost for your tax filing. Your final estimated cost may be higher if your business requires or chooses additional services.
How do I file with a Block Advisor tax pro?
On the left-side menu, click Perks, then scroll down to the More to explore section and select H&R Block.
chunks.category: Help Center > Accounting > Key accounting concepts

chunks.title: [US] Tax filing with Block Advisors
chunks.content:
For Schedule C returns: Follow the prompts to set up your Block Advisors account. Assign transactions to the relevant IRS categories and upload necessary documents. A small business tax pro from Block Advisors will prepare your return.
For multi-member LLCs, S-Corps, or C-Corps: Add your tax pro as a collaborator in your Wave account using Tax pro (Block Advisors). They will use your Wave reports to prepare your return.
What can a Block Advisor tax pro collaborator access in my Wave account?
Block Advisor tax pro collaborators have read-only access to:
Reports
Accounting
Sales
Purchases
Payroll (if applicable)
User management
Do I need to schedule an in-person appointment with my tax pro?
No, there is no need for an in-person meeting. Your tax pro can file virtually, providing access to their expertise from anywhere.
How do I add a tax pro to my Wave account?
To learn how to add a tax pro to your Wave account, read Invite or remove collaborators from your business.
What do I have to do to file by myself?
Create your Block Advisors account: Start with personal questions to determine your filing status.
Verify business information: Follow the prompts to confirm or complete your business details.
Assign income and expenses: Ensure all your transactions from Wave are categorized correctly. Review any uncategorized items.
Complete additional information: If necessary, provide details on expenses like mileage or home office deductions.
If you have questions while filing, use Online Assist for unlimited live help from Block Advisors tax experts.
What data is sent from Wave to Block Advisors?
Wave sends the following information to Block Advisors:
Basic information such as your business name and address
Balances of all categories on your Profit & Loss report for the entire tax year will be added to the Schedule C section of your 1040.
chunks.category: Help Center > Accounting > Key accounting concepts

chunks.title: [US] Tax filing with Block Advisors
chunks.content:
Wave sends the cash basis Profit & Loss balances, which is the most common for small businesses. Check your previous year's Schedule C to confirm you file this way. Look for question F: Accounting Method at the top of page 1. If the box next to (1) Cash is checked, you’re filing correctly.
Can I file with Wave and Block Advisors if I haven’t categorized all of my transactions?
You can start your return without categorizing all transactions. However, you will receive reminders to finish this process. Follow the prompts to return to your Transactions page in Wave and categorize any uncategorized transactions.
After categorization, click re-import Wave data on your tax return to ensure the transaction categories are updated on your return. Any accounting adjustments made on Block Advisors are overwritten if you re-import data.
Can I complete tax filing if I haven’t reconciled my accounts?
Wave strongly recommends you reconcile your accounts before filing to ensure they are accurate. However, you can still file with Block Advisors without reconciling your accounts.
chunks.category: Help Center > Accounting > Key accounting concepts

chunks.title: Scan and upload your receipts
chunks.content:
The receipts scan feature allows you to capture and upload images of receipts on the mobile app, upload receipt files in your web browser, and forward your digital receipts via email. Each receipt you upload automatically creates a corresponding expense transaction in your accounting.
The receipts scan feature is available with a subscription to Wave’s Receipts Plan or Pro Plan. To manage receipts without the receipts scan feature, you can Add or delete an attachment on a transaction.
Scan and upload a receipt in the Wave mobile app
Scan and upload a receipt in your web browser
Scan and upload a receipt in the Wave mobile app
Log in to the Wave mobile app.
On the bottom menu, tap Accounting > Receipts.
Tap the camera icon at the top right. If you're uploading your first receipt, tap Scan receipt instead.
Take a picture of the receipt. The first time you take a picture you’ll need to tap Allow Access to give the app permission to access your camera. If your receipt is long or double-sided:
At the bottom, tap Long Receipt.
Take a picture of the top or front of the receipt.
Tap Next Section.
Take a photo of the bottom or back of the receipt.
To take pictures of multiple receipts, tap Add on the bottom.
Tap Done.
Once the image is uploaded successfully, it is added to your list of recent scans. An expense transaction is created automatically on your Transactions page.
Wave automatically merges duplicate expense transactions with the created receipt transactions. Find more details in Automated bookkeeping with auto-updates.
To verify the information is correct, or to add or edit any details, tap on the receipt. You can edit the date, amount, account, and category, and add notes. Once you have verified the transaction details, you can mark the receipt as reviewed by tapping the Mark as reviewed button.
Scan and upload a receipt in your web browser
You can upload up to 10 files at a time in JPG, GIF, PNG or PDF formats. Each file can be up to 5MB in size.

chunks.title: Scan and upload your receipts
chunks.content:
To upload a receipt from the Receipts page:
Log in to your account at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Receipts.
Click Select files, then upload your receipt file(s) from the file browser.
To upload a receipt from the Transactions page:
Log in to your account at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Accounting > Transactions.
At the top of the page, click Add transaction > Scan receipt.
Upload your receipt file(s).
Once the file is scanned and uploaded successfully, it is added to your list of recent scans. An expense transaction is created automatically on your Transactions page.
To verify the information is correct, or to add or edit any details, click on the receipt. This opens the transaction on your Transactions page where you can edit the details.

chunks.title: [US] Frequently asked questions about direct deposit
chunks.content:
When do I have to approve payroll by if I am using direct deposit?
The funding timeline is four business days from the date you approve the payroll if you approve it before 8:00 PM Eastern. For example, if you want your employees to be paid on Friday, you must approve the payroll on Monday before 8:00 PM Eastern.
If there are bank holidays between the date of approval and payday, the timeline will be affected. Learn how bank holidays affect payroll direct deposit timelines.
What if I don’t approve my payroll on time?
If you don’t approve your payroll in time for your expected payday, pay your employees outside of Wave. To ensure the payroll's information is recorded in Wave, turn off direct deposit for each employee, then approve your payroll and transfer the funds outside of Wave.
Wave may be able to expedite your direct deposit with the help of our Support Team. To request this, open Mave, Wave’s automated chatbot, and type human support payroll expedite, then provide the pay period dates.
When can I change my funding account?
You can change your funding account (the bank account where the payroll withdrawal is made), as long as the current date is after the payday of the last payroll you approved. Once you approve a payroll with direct deposit, your funding account information is locked until the day after payday. This is to ensure the payroll is processed correctly.
Is my information secure?
The security of your information is important to us. Rest assured that your direct deposit information is protected by our security policy. 
How do I add my funding account when I can't find my bank?
If the bank you are trying to add is not available, it is not currently supported by Plaid. Instead, add your bank account manually.
Entering your details manually is only an option for Wave's payroll and payment features, and can’t be used to import transactions. To add transactions manually into Wave, use Wave Connect or upload statements instead.

chunks.title: [US] Frequently asked questions about direct deposit
chunks.content:
How do I add my credit union to fund my payroll?
Credit union account details like the routing and account number length can vary based on the credit union.
To ensure you connect your business account correctly, enter a symbol into the search bar, then select Use your bank routing and account numbers. Enter your routing and account number, which you can find on a void cheque or pre-authorized debit form.
Account statements from credit unions may only show part of the account number for the purpose of direct deposit or electronic funds transfers.
If you don't have a void cheque or pre-authorized debit form available, contact your credit union directly for the correct details.

chunks.title: Advisor bar
chunks.content:
The Advisor bar allows you to view outstanding bookkeeping tasks, business checklists, Wave Advisor tips, and explore Help Center articles.

chunks.title: Integrate Wave with other apps
chunks.content:
As of May 26, 2025, all businesses in Wave require a Pro Plan or Wave Advisors bookkeeping subscription to connect with and maintain existing connections with Partner integrations and Make. Wave integrations are not affected. Learn more about Wave’s plans or how to subscribe.
Integrations do not include automatic bank transaction imports, users or tax filing with Block Advisors.
As a thank you for being a part of the Wave community, users who create a new account with Make will get 2 months of free access to Make. Users who create a new account with MinuteDock get 50% off their MinuteDock subscription for 3 months.
  Integrations allow you to connect your Wave account with other tools you use to manage your business. The Integrations page lists available apps. To connect or complete tasks with an app:
Log in to your Wave account at waveapps.com.
Click on your business name at the top right corner, then click Integrations.
Click Use workflow or the relevant action button next to the action you want to use.
Select the business profile to connect to.
To confirm you want to allow the app to connect to your Wave account, select Allow access.

Partner Integrations: available integrations that are built and supported by the partner app provider, such as Driversnote.
Make: an integration service that allows you to create automated connections without any coding. This means you can streamline processes like adding new customers to an email list or receiving alerts for new invoices.
Make builds and maintain the connections. For help with your integrations, contact Make support.

chunks.title: Add a deposit request to an estimate
chunks.content:
This feature is for Pro Plan subscribers and businesses using Wave’s online payments feature.
Adding a deposit request on an estimate helps secure funds for your services before your business completes any work. Deposits can be paid using a credit card in your business currency.
You can only add one deposit request per estimate.
To add a deposit request to an estimate:
Log in to your account at waveapps.com.
Find and open your selected estimate, or create a new estimate.
Under Total, click Add deposit request.
Enter the deposit amount as a dollar value or percentage. The deposit cannot be more than the estimate’s total.
To require a deposit payment, select the checkbox next to Require customer to pay deposit online before marking it as accepted.
You can only require a deposit if your business is actively using online payments.
Click Save and continue to save your estimate draft.
Click Approve draft to finalize the estimate.
Learn how to record a manual deposit payment on an estimate or understand how a customer makes a payment.
If you convert an estimate to an invoice before receiving a deposit, the deposit request will not appear on the invoice.

chunks.title: Remove a manual deposit payment on an estimate
chunks.content:
This feature is for Pro Plan subscribers and businesses using Wave’s online payments feature.
To remove a deposit payment made using Wave’s online payment feature, refund your customer.
To remove a manually recorded payment:
Log in to Wave at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Sales & Payments > Estimates.
Locate and click on the estimate.
In the Accept section, locate the manually recorded payment.
Click Remove payment, then in the pop-up window, click Yes, remove payment.

chunks.title: Record a manual deposit payment on an estimate
chunks.content:
This feature is for Pro Plan subscribers and businesses using Wave’s online payments feature. 
You can only record deposit payments directly on an estimate.
You cannot record a deposit payment on an estimate after you convert it into an invoice. Instead, manually add an invoice payment to record the deposit.
To record a deposit payment on an estimate:
Log in to your account at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Sales & Payments > Estimates.
Locate the estimate.
On the right, click the dropdown arrow, then click Record a deposit.
Enter the details of the deposit, then click Submit. If the estimate has not yet been accepted, click Submit & mark as accepted.
If your customer has not yet accepted the estimate, when you record the payment, it will be marked as accepted. You can record full or partial deposit payments.
A deposit transaction will appear on your Transactions page in the customer’s credit account. Editing or deleting the transaction will affect the deposit on the estimate and the recorded funds in their credit account. Track customer deposit payments in your customer credit report.

chunks.title: Turn off two-factor authentication (2FA)
chunks.content:
Wave requires payroll and online payments users to have 2FA turned on. Once 2FA is required on your account, if you turn it off, you will be signed out of Wave and asked to set it up again.
If you aren’t using payroll or online payments, 2FA can be turned off at any time. To turn off 2FA:
Click your business name in the top right corner, then click Profile Settings.
In the Profile menu, click Password & Security.
Next to your active method, click Turn off.
In the pop-up, click Turn off… to confirm.
You will see an Inactive label under the 2FA sign-in method you chose. To reactivate 2FA, turn two-factor authentication on again.

chunks.title: Understand an estimate status
chunks.content:
Statuses indicate the latest action that has been taken by you or your customer, so you can track the progress of your estimates.
An estimate can only show one status at a time. When a new action is taken, the status updates.
Draft: The estimate has been created and saved as a draft.
Saved: The draft estimate is approved but not yet sent to the customer.
Sent: The estimate has been sent to the customer.
Viewed: The customer has viewed the estimate.
Accepted: The customer has accepted the estimate.
Accepting an estimate is part of Wave’s Pro Plan. Learn about Wave’s plans.
Converted: The estimate has been converted to an invoice.
Expired: The Valid Until date of the estimate has passed.
To accept or send an expired estimate, or convert it to an invoice, edit the Valid Until date to a future date. Learn how to Edit, delete, or duplicate an estimate.

chunks.content:

On the bottom menu, tap Sales Invoices.
Tap the All tab.
Under the Payments section, tap the arrow next to the payments made.
Tap the refund or credit, then tap the three dots at the top right.
To edit, tap Edit, make the changes, then tap Save.
To delete, tap Delete payment, then, to confirm, tap Delete payment in the pop-up.

chunks.title: Reconcile your books
chunks.content:
The Reconciliation page is only available on the web version of Wave.
Reconciliation helps you find missing or incorrect transactions in your accounts by matching your bank statement with the transactions in Wave. This helps you maintain the accuracy of your financial records.
To reconcile an account, open or create a reconciliation period, then match the transactions in Wave to the transactions on your bank statement. Your bank statement should list all transactions for the date range and the closing balance.
Learn how to reconcile your books with a video.
Create or open a reconciliation period
Match your transactions
Create or open a reconciliation period
You cannot create a new reconciliation period for an account if it has an existing unreconciled period.
To create a reconciliation period or open an existing one:
On the left-side menu, click Accounting > Transactions.
At the top right of the page, next to Reconciliation, switch the reconciliation toggle to On.
Select the account you want to reconcile. If you have filtered to a specific account already, you will only see existing reconciliation periods for that account.
To create a new period, enter the end date and closing balance of the bank statement, then click Start reconciling.
To open a reconciled period, select the period or click the pencil icon.
To continue reconciling a period in progress, click Continue reconciling. This opens your last reconciliation period.
Click Start reconciling.
To return to the all transactions view, switch the reconciliation toggle to off.
Match your transactions
If you can’t find a matched transaction, it may be in another reconciliation period.
If your Closing balance is the same as your Matched balance, a pop-up will appear. To have Wave match all transactions, click Reconcile automatically. To match transactions yourself, click Reconcile manually.

chunks.title: Reconcile your books
chunks.content:
The number of unmatched transactions, the Closing balance from your bank statement, the Matched balance in Wave, and the Difference between the two balances are at the top of your reconciliation period.
To mark a transaction as matched, under the Match column, click the balance icon. To unmatch a transaction, click the balance icon again.
As you match transactions, the Matched balance and the Difference amount will update.
The Difference amount will be zero once all transactions have been matched and there are no discrepancies between transactions and your bank statement. Click End reconciliation to complete the period.
If there is a discrepancy between your balances, you'll see the difference amount under Difference. Learn how to fix an unreconciled period.
To leave a reconciliation period, at the top left, click Back to reconciliation history. Your work automatically saves. To continue reconciling later, return to the reconciliation page for the account and click Continue reconciling.
On the all transactions view, transactions that have been matched in a reconciliation period have a balance icon to their left.

Understand your income by customer report

Understand your income by customer report
The income by customer report helps you track income from individual customers, including both paid and unpaid amounts, within a specific time period.
Your report has 3 columns:
Customers: Customers with an invoice or sales transaction attached to them. Customers with only estimates aren't included.
All income: The total amount of all attached invoices and any attached income transactions for that customer in your selected date range.
Paid income: The total amount a customer has paid through invoices and attached income transactions for the selected date range.
At the bottom of the report are the sums of all income and paid income for all customers.
If an invoice was sent outside the selected date range, but paid within it, the amount is only included in the customer's Paid income column.
To view detailed transactions for a customer, click an amount in their columns. Clicking an All income amount opens the account transactions report on an accrual basis. Clicking a Paid income amount opens the account transactions report on a cash basis.
Learn more in View and understand your account transactions (general ledger) report.

At the bottom of the report are the sum totals of all purchases and paid purchases to all vendors.

chunks.content:

View your aged payables report
Understand the aged payables report

Overviews of bill payments coming due and the overdue bills are on your business dashboard.
On the left-side menu, click Reports.
In the Customers section, click Aged Payables.
Select the As of date.
Click Update Report.
Learn how to Export a report.
Understand your aged payables report
The aged payables report shows the unpaid bills owed to your vendors or contractors, categorized by how overdue they are. This report helps you track and manage outstanding liabilities.
The As of date is the starting point of the report. Any bills listed as overdue are considered overdue as of that specific date. If a bill was paid after your selected As of date, it will still appear as overdue on the current report.
To see the most up-to-date unpaid amounts, use today’s date for your As of date.
Each row in the report lists overdue bill totals for one vendor. Your report has 6 columns:
Not Yet Overdue: Bills that are not yet overdue.
30 or Less: Bills less than 30 days overdue.
31-60: Bills that are 31 to 60 days overdue.
61-90: Bills that are 61 to 90 days overdue.
91 or More: Bills more than 91 days overdue.
Total Unpaid: The total overdue amount for that specific vendor.
At the bottom of the report are the total amounts owed to all vendors for each column.
Overpaid bills will not reduce the amount owed or overdue to that vendor.

chunks.content:

Understand your account balances report
The account balances report shows the balances and total money movement for each account in Wave within the selected time period.
Your account balances report is split into sections based on your Chart of Accounts tabs. Each row in the report lists a different account. There are 6 columns that list:
Account: The name of the financial account.
Starting Balance: The amount of money in that account on the first day of your selected date range.
Debit: The total amount of money that was withdrawn from the account during your selected date range. This amount represents your purchases, bill payments, and expenses.
Credit: The total amount of money that was deposited into the account during your selected date range. This amount represents your invoice payments, estimate deposits, and sales.
Net Movement: The overall change in the account's balance. This amount is calculated by subtracting the account's Debits from its Credits. A positive number means the account gained money, and a negative number means the account lost money.
Ending Balance: The current account balance. This amount is calculated by adding or subtracting the Net Movement amount from the Starting Balance.
At the bottom of each section are the total amounts for each column.

Understand the account transactions report
The account transactions report lists details of all transactions for each account in your Chart of Accounts. This is the main report for all financial activity, grouped by account. Each transaction is recorded in two accounts: where the money came from, and where it’s going. This ensures that your books are always in balance.
Use this report to review your financial activity, account balances, and transaction history during a selected time period.
On your account transactions report, you can view the:
Account name and where the account can be found in your Chart of Accounts
Starting and ending balances for the selected date range
Transactions within the account for the selected date range
Debit or credit amounts of each transaction
Total debit and credit balances for each account

chunks.title: Invoice statuses
chunks.content:
An invoice is assigned one status at a time. This status is updated when the invoice meets the next step's criteria:
Draft: Invoices saved as drafts.
Unsent: Invoices that have not been sent through Wave or marked as sent.
Sent: Invoices that have been sent through Wave or marked as sent.
Viewed: Invoices your customers have viewed.
Partial: Invoices that have been partially paid and have a balance due.
Paid: Fully paid invoices.
Overpaid: Invoices with a negative amount due.
Overdue: Unpaid or partially paid invoices past their due date.

chunks.title: Fix an unreconciled period
chunks.content:
The Reconciliation page is only available on the web version of Wave.
A reconciliation period may become unreconciled if a transaction is edited or merged, or if a payment is edited. If you make changes to a transaction, invoice, or estimate, a pop-up will notify you if it affects a reconciled period.
Reconciliation periods with discrepancies are highlighted in red. A red banner above the reconciled periods shows the difference between the ending balance and starting balance of the two most recent periods.
To fix the unreconciled period:
In the red banner, click Fix it.
Compare your transactions in Wave with your bank statement for the same time period.
To resolve common discrepancies:
Missing transactions: Click Add Transaction at the top of the page.
Incorrect transactions: Click on the transaction to edit the information.
Duplicate transactions: Select the checkboxes to the left of the duplicate transactions. At the top of the transactions list, click the merge icon.
Incorrect statement balance: Click the pencil icon beside the Closing balance amount. Enter the correct closing balance and click Save.
Pending transactions: If a transaction is in a reconciliation period but not on your bank statement, Wave may be using the transaction date instead of the posting date. Click End reconciliation, then Reconcile period anyway. You will match this transaction in the next reconciliation period.
Extra transactions: If you created a transaction by mistake, click the checkbox to the left of the transaction, then click the trash can icon to delete it.

chunks.title: View and understand reconciliation statuses
chunks.content:
Reconciliation is only available on the web version of Wave.
View your reconciliation summary page
To view the reconciliation status of all your accounts, view your reconciliation summary page. To view your reconciliation summary page:
On the left-side menu, click Accounting > Transactions.
At the top right, next to Reconciliation, switch the reconciliation toggle to On.
You will see a list of all of your accounts, their current balance total, and their reconciliation status.
Understand a reconciliation status
When reviewing your reconciliation, each account shows a reconciliation status:
Not reconciled: This is the first reconciliation period for that account. To reconcile your transactions, create a reconciliation period.
Reconciled: Your bank balance matches the Wave balance in all reconciliation periods. To reconcile new transactions, create a new reconciliation period.
Needs attention: There is a reconciliation period where your Wave balance does not match the bank statement balance. The affected reconciliation period is highlighted in red. Learn how to fix an unreconciled accounting period.
In progress: You started reconciling your account, but did not finish. You can continue to reconcile your account.

On the left-side menu, click Accounting > Transactions.
At the top right, next to Reconciliation, switch the reconciliation toggle to On.
Select the account with the reconciliation period to be deleted.
To the right of the reconciliation period, click the dropdown arrow, then click Delete.

chunks.title: Frequently asked questions about the new online payments experience
chunks.content:
Over the next several weeks, Wave is updating our online payments experience. As we update, some customers might require a review of their payment account information. This is a standard step as a provider of regulated financial services to ensure compliance with federal regulations.
If you received an email and an in-app notice to update your information, please review and update any necessary information using the link provided by the specified date to avoid interruptions to your payments.
Why do I have to update my online payment details?
Wave is investing in a new infrastructure to bring you a better online payments experience and help us deliver new features to support your business. As a provider of financial services, Wave is obligated to comply with regulations and ensure our customers’ online payment information is regularly up to date and secure. We ask our customers to update or review their information from time to time to keep compliant.
Once you submit your information, there will be a short pause in payment processing while your information is processed. Once your information is updated, you’ll be able to continue accepting online payments again.
What happens if I don’t update my online payment information?
Some accounts will require quick reviews to ensure all information is up-to-date. This should only take a few minutes.
If you do not update your online payment information within 45 days of receiving your notice for updates, your payments will be temporarily paused. A banner in-app at the top of your Wave account will notify you that your payments will be paused.
You can update your information at any time to reactivate and continue processing your payments.
I’ve updated my online payments information. How long will it take for me to be able to use online payments again?

chunks.title: Frequently asked questions about the new online payments experience
chunks.content:
While we can’t guarantee an exact time for information processing, approvals should happen shortly after submission. If additional updates, corrections, or further reviews are needed, this can impact the timeline.
I received an email and an in-app notice that Wave is requesting more information. What happened?
You’ll receive a notice if there are any issues with updating your account. This can happen for many reasons, such as the information was input incorrectly or did not match the system.
Follow the directions in your email or review the directions in-app for updates required. If you have any issues updating your online payments information, our Support team can help. To reach them, open Mave, Wave’s automated chatbot, and request a Support Agent.
What will happen to my data?
Your data will be kept secure with Wave. For more information on privacy and security, please review our Terms of Service. Your information will be updated through a secure site that enables Wave to update your account information successfully.
You will continue to have access to your current payment information and payments-related bookkeeping.
Will this impact my existing payments?
For the majority of our customers, there should be no interruption to your existing workflow and payment processing. You will receive an email with the subject line “Action required: please verify your payment details”.
If you do not update your information as requested by the provided date, your online payments will be paused. You will also see a prompt in-app notifying you of this and how to complete the outstanding actions required to continue using payments.
While your payment details are being updated and verified, accepting online payments will be temporarily paused. The verification process should be relatively quick, but if any additional information is required, we ask that you make updates in a timely manner to ensure there is no interruption to your payments experience.

chunks.title: Review and respond to a chargeback (New online payments experience)
chunks.content:
Review a chargeback
Respond to a chargeback
Review a chargeback
Once a chargeback has been initiated by your customer, you can review the details and where you are in the dispute process at any time. Learn more about the chargeback process.
You cannot issue a refund for a payment where the cardholder has initiated a chargeback.
To review a chargeback:
Log in at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Sales & Payments > Payments.
Click the payment with the status Chargeback.
In the pop-up window, you can view the amount credited from your bank account, the original payment method, and the chargeback status. Beneath the status is how many days you have left to respond to the chargeback.
If you miss the deadline to respond to the chargeback, it will automatically be accepted.
To view the affected invoice, click View invoice.
Respond to a chargeback
If more than one chargeback has been initiated on the same invoice, you will have the option to respond differently to each one. There are 3 ways to respond to a chargeback:
Accept the chargeback
Have the customer drop their chargeback
Dispute the chargeback
Accept the chargeback
Accepting a chargeback means that you agree the charge to your customer was not intentional. This does not affect your credit score or reflect on documents outside of Wave.
To accept the chargeback, no further action is required. Your customer will keep their payment, and the bank will keep the $7 fee.
Have the customer drop their chargeback
If your customer drops their chargeback, you must notify Wave. Learn What to do if your customer wants to drop a chargeback.
Dispute the chargeback
To dispute the chargeback, you must prove that the reason the customer initiated the chargeback is not true. Learn more in Understand the chargeback process.
To dispute the chargeback:
Open the affected transaction on the Payments page.
In the pop-up window, click Appeal chargeback.
If there are multiple chargebacks, select the checkbox for the ones you want to dispute, then click Appeal.

chunks.title: Change from a Receipts Plan to Pro Plan subscription

You can change your subscription from the Receipts Plan to the Pro Plan at any time.
When you upgrade your plan from Receipts to Pro, you get access to Pro Plan features immediately. Your new billing date will be the day you make the upgrade. Any remaining balance paid for the Receipts Plan will automatically be credited toward your new Pro Plan.
You must switch to the Pro Plan from the same platform (web browser or mobile app) where you subscribed to the Receipts Plan.

Change from Receipts Plan to Pro Plan in the mobile app

Select the Monthly or Annual tab to choose your subscription period, then select Upgrade to Pro.
Confirm that you are subscribing from the correct business, then select Continue.
Enter your details and payment information. If you have a coupon code, enter the code and select Apply.

Under Subscriptions, tap Upgrade.
Select the Monthly or Annual tab to choose your subscription period, then tap Upgrade to Pro.

chunks.title: Refund a customer payment (New online payments experience)
chunks.content:
You can send either a full or partial refund. Always issue refunds to the original customer and payment method to avoid disputes with the cardholder’s bank.
Refunds to credit cards take 3 - 5 business days
Refunds to bank accounts take 5 - 10 business days
Refund a payment
Refund eligibility
Refund a payment
Log in at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Sales & Payments > Payments.
Click on the payment you want to refund.
Click Refund payment in the pop-up.
To send a partial refund, select Enter refund amount, then enter the amount. To send a full refund, select Full refund.
Wave refunds the processing fees they collected on a pro-rated basis, and the remaining balance is withdrawn from your payout account.
Choose a reason for the refund.
Include any relevant notes in the notes field.
Click the Refund button.
If successful, you'll see the status Refund processing next to the payment. Once the refund has been sent to your customer, you'll see the status Refunded.
If your bank fails to process the refund, you'll see the status Refund failed. If this happens, follow the steps above again to refund the payment.
If you refunded an invoice payment, the invoice will appear as overdue. If you do not expect another payment, write off the invoice.
Refund eligibility
You cannot refund a payment that is currently undergoing a payment dispute (chargeback).
Payments made over 120 days ago need to be refunded by our Support Team. Open Mave, Wave’s automated chatbot, and type human support refund over 120 days. Provide the invoice date, invoice number, and amount to be refunded.

chunks.title: View your payments (New online payments experience)
chunks.content:
A payment refers to the money you receive when your customers pay an invoice through Wave.
View your payments
Log in at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Sales & Payments > Payments.
To view payments made before the new payments experience upgrade, click View classic payments.
To filter or search for a payment you can select a Date range, Sale type and Customer, and search by invoice number.
To remove a filter, click the cross next to it.
Click on a payment to see the processing timeline, breakdown of processing fees, and reference number.
To view the invoice details, click View invoice.
Learn what each payment status means in Understand your payment statuses.

chunks.title: Understand your payment statuses
chunks.content:
Payment statuses
Processing: A payment has been made by your customer. It is being processed or has been accepted and is waiting to be paid out
Deposited: The payment has been deposited in your payout account
Declined: The payment couldn’t be accepted and no funds have been moved
Refunded: The payment has been refunded to your customer
Partial refund: A custom amount of the payment has been refunded to your customer
Refund failed: The refund wasn't processed and the funds have been returned to your account
On hold: The payment is being assessed by our Risk Team
Chargeback: A customer has disputed the payment and a chargeback is in process
Cancellation processing: The payment cancellation is being processed
Cancelled: The payment has been successfully cancelled
Cancellation failed: The payment wasn't successfully cancelled and will continue processing

chunks.title: Cancel a payment (New online payments experience)
chunks.content:
You can cancel a payment if it is still processing and has not yet been accepted. In the Timeline section of the Payment details, the status will show Payment processing.
To cancel a payment:
Log in at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Sales & Payments > Payments.
Click on the payment you want to cancel.
Click Cancel payment in the pop-up.
To confirm, click Yes, cancel payment.
If successful, the status of the payment will change to Cancellation processing. Processing usually takes a few minutes. Once processed, the status will update to Cancelled.
If the cancellation doesn't process, you'll see the status Cancellation failed. If this happens, follow the steps above to try again as soon as possible, otherwise, your payment will continue processing.
Once the payment is processed, you cannot cancel it. If this happens, you can refund the payment instead.

chunks.title: Charge a customer credit card (New online payments experience)

You can collect invoice payments using Wave in two ways: by sending an invoice for online payment or by manually charging your customer's credit card.
International payments: You can accept invoice payments from credit cards issued outside your business's country. The cardholder's bank will complete the payment in the invoice currency and handle any currency conversion.

chunks.title: [US] How Etsy transaction bookkeeping works in Wave
chunks.content:
The Etsy integration is available in business profiles based in the US with an active Pro Plan subscription.
Wave automatically imports your Etsy transactions that have finished processing every 24 hours.
Etsy accounts created in Wave
Sales bookkeeping
Etsy fee bookkeeping
Etsy accounts created in Wave
When you first connect to the integration, Wave creates all Etsy-related accounts automatically. These accounts are:
Etsy Product Sales
Etsy Transaction Fees
Etsy Payment Processing Fees
Etsy Service Income
Etsy Discount account
Etsy Advertising and Promotion
Etsy Listing Fees
Etsy Shipping
Etsy Subscription/Software Fees
Sales bookkeeping
Each individual sale is recorded in the Etsy Money in Transit account. This is a single split deposit transaction that records the total sale amount and the different fees categorized to their relevant expense accounts. The order number is also included in the description and the link to the order in Etsy is in the Notes section.
All income not from a sale is recorded under the account Etsy Service Income. Any discounts received are recorded in the Etsy Discount account.
The Etsy integration doesn't import operational transactions like inventory or fulfillment tracking, or payouts you receive directly from Etsy.
Once you receive the payout for a sale, you must manually categorize the payment as a transfer from your Etsy Money in Transit account:
Open the Transactions page.
Find your imported payout transaction, or create a new income transaction.
Select the category Transfer from a Bank, Credit Card or Loan > Etsy Money in Transit. If you’re creating a new transaction, fill in the remaining details.
Select Save.
Wave automatically creates the matching transfer transaction under the Etsy Money in Transit account.
chunks.category: Help Center > Manage Your Account > Integrations

chunks.title: [US] How Etsy transaction bookkeeping works in Wave
chunks.content:
Multiple payments and fees that are processed close together may be bundled into one payout. This means your fees may sometimes be greater than your income from sales. In this case, Etsy may charge the difference to your bank account. Categorize this withdrawal transaction as a Transfer to a Bank, Credit Card or Loan > Etsy Money in Transit.
How does Wave handle the sales taxes?
Due to Marketplace Facilitator Laws in the US, Etsy must collect and remit sales taxes directly to state authorities on your behalf. This means sales tax is not included in your imported transactions, to prevent incorrectly adding tax liabilities and inflating your income.
Etsy fee bookkeeping
Fees not associated with a specific sale are recorded as a single transaction, categorized to the relevant expense account.

chunks.title: Troubleshoot customers not receiving invoices sent through Wave
chunks.content:
Invoices sent through a shared link or PDF are not traceable by Wave. If a customer is not receiving documents sent outside of Wave, troubleshoot with your customer or email service provider.
If your customers are not receiving the invoices you send through Wave, there are a few troubleshooting steps you can take:
Have your customers check the filters in their email account and their junk/spam folders.
Have them add @waveapps.com to their address book.
