You can also send invoices to your customer using a different method.
If you continue to have issues with customers receiving invoice emails, open Mave, Wave’s automated chatbot, and type my customer isn't getting invoices. Mave will help collect any relevant details and direct you to the appropriate support. Learn how to open Mave in Get support with Wave.

chunks.title: Resolve differences between your Wave balances and bank balances
chunks.content:
If your balances do not match, this may be due to a few reasons:
Delayed bank transaction imports
Funds in transit
Unreconciled accounts
Starting balances
Inflated income accounts
Inconsistent amounts for the same account
Delayed bank transaction imports
This feature is part of Wave’s Pro Plan. Learn more about Wave’s plans or how to subscribe.
If you have connected your bank accounts in Wave to import transactions, you will notice that imports only happen at fixed intervals, not in real time. Once your transactions are imported, check to see if your balances match.
Funds in transit
When you accept a check payment from a customer or write a check for a vendor, there is a period before the funds are deposited or withdrawn from your bank account. This is when the money is considered in transit. If you record the payment in Wave while the funds are in transit, your balances may not match. Learn how to bookkeep an undeposited check.
If you have recorded an undeposited check payment to a Money in Transit account, it may now be cleared, causing your balances to be mismatched. To resolve this, bookkeep the check as deposited.
Reconcile your accounts to a date before the check was recorded to verify that your account balances match.
Unreconciled accounts
If you have not reconciled your accounts, there could be missing or duplicate transactions in your Wave account. When you compare your bank statement with the transactions in Wave, you can identify and correct any differences. Learn how to reconcile your accounts
Starting balances
If your accounts are reconciled, check if you have a starting balance entered for your account. A starting balance represents the amount in the bank account before the period you start with Wave. An incorrect or missing starting balance can result in an incorrect account balance in Wave.
Inflated income accounts
If you notice an inflated amount for income accounts when using cash basis, check if you have edited your invoices to add any negative line items.

chunks.title: Resolve differences between your Wave balances and bank balances
chunks.content:
A negative line item may have been used to prevent an invoice from showing as overdue after recording a refund on the invoice. Delete the negative line item and correct the overdue balance by writing off the invoice.
Inconsistent amounts for the same account
There are rare occasions when your Wave pages may not communicate with each other. This causes reports in Wave to display inconsistent amounts for the same account across different reports. In cases like this, a data refresh may be required.
Future-dated transactions will not be included in the account balances on the Transactions page or the Reconciliation page. However, the transactions will be included in the Account Transactions report.
You may need a data refresh if:
There are different amounts for the same account when you compare reports. The report types should be consistent when comparing reports.
The balance widget at the top of your Transaction page isn’t updating when adding new transactions
The Wave balance on your Reconciliation page does not match the balance on your Account Transactions report for the same account and timeframe.
The Wave balance after the last transaction entered in a reconciliation period does not match the Wave balance at the top of the page.
If you notice any of the above issues, our support team may need to refresh your data. Open Mave, Wave’s automated chatbot, and type human support inconsistent report balances. Mave will help collect any relevant details and direct you to the appropriate support.

chunks.title: View and understand your aged receivables report
chunks.content:
The aged receivables report is only available on the web version of Wave.
View your aged receivables report
Understand your aged receivables report
View your aged receivables report

On the left-side menu, click Reports.
In the Customers section, click Aged Receivables.
Select the As of date.
Click Update Report.
Learn how to Export a report.
Understand your aged receivables report
The aged receivables report helps you track and manage outstanding invoice payments. It shows your unpaid and overdue invoices, categorized by how overdue they are.
The As of date is the starting point of the report. Any invoices listed as overdue are considered overdue as of that specific date. If an invoice was paid after your selected As of date, it will still appear as overdue on the current report.
To see the most up-to-date unpaid amounts, use today’s date for your As of date.
Each row in the report lists overdue invoice totals for one customer. Your report has 6 columns:
Not Yet Overdue: Invoices that are unpaid but are not yet overdue.
30 or Less: Invoices less than 30 days overdue.
31-60: Invoices that are 31 to 60 days overdue.
61-90: Invoices that are 61 to 90 days overdue.
91 or More: Invoices more than 91 days overdue.
Total Unpaid: The total overdue amount for that specific customer.
At the bottom of the report are the total amounts due from all customers for each column.
Your aged receivables report may not always balance with your accounts receivable account. The accounts receivable account is an asset account that shows the money your business is owed. When you approve an invoice draft, the accounts receivable account is debited, increasing the balance in the account. When you record a payment for an invoice, the accounts receivable account is credited, decreasing the balance in the account. The aged receivable report only shows the unpaid and overdue invoices, which could result in a balance discrepancy.

Receipts: This export contains a ZIP file with all uploaded receipt images in their original file types.

Employee profiles: Your employees' profile information
Pay stubs: All employees' pay stubs

chunks.title: Wave Advisors' services
chunks.content:
Wave Advisors are Wave’s in-house professionals specializing in bookkeeping, accounting, and payroll setup. Advisors can take care of your bookkeeping for you, or coach you on how to do it yourself.
Your advisor can add themselves remotely to your Wave business as an admin collaborator to assist with providing services. Learn more in our terms of service.
A Wave advisor will never ask for the password to your Wave account.
Wave Advisors’ services are only for assistance with features within Wave.
Bookkeeping services
Accounting coaching
Payroll coaching
Bookkeeping services
Bookkeeping services are not available in Quebec, Canada.
Wave Advisors' bookkeeping services are offered on a recurring monthly basis. You are assigned an in-house bookkeeper who helps keep your accounting up-to-date. Your bookkeeper helps with transaction categorization and reconciliation, and provides monthly review calls.
Bookkeeping services include a Pro Plan subscription without the Receipts feature.
Accounting coaching
Wave Advisors’ accounting coaching is a service that sets you up with an understanding of your own Wave accounting. You are assigned an in-house accounting coach who will ensure you have set up your Wave accounting properly and can manage your bookkeeping yourself.
Payroll coaching
Wave Advisors’ payroll coaching is a service to help you set up and understand your payroll in Wave. You are assigned an in-house payroll coach who will help set up your payroll account, understand how your business’s payroll taxes work, and assist you in successfully running your first payroll.
For more information on Wave Advisor services, pricing, or to book a call, see Personalized help with Wave Advisors.

chunks.title: Send an estimate through Wave
chunks.content:
Businesses that accept online payments or subscribe to Wave’s Pro Plan can send estimates directly through Wave. Learn about Wave’s plans and how to subscribe or how to set up online payments.
Send an estimate through Wave in your web browser
Send an estimate through Wave in the Wave mobile app
Send an estimate through Wave in your web browser
Log in to your Wave account at waveapps.com.
On the left-side menu, click Sales & Payments > Estimates.
Click the Send button to the right of the estimate you want to send. Or, click on the estimate to open it, then click Send estimate.
To send the estimate through Wave, fill in the required fields:
To send the estimate from an alternate verified email address saved under your business profile, click on your email address in the From field and choose from the list. To add another email address to your business profile, follow these steps.
You can edit the subject line, or the message that will appear on the body of the email your customer receives.
With a Pro Plan subscription, you can customize the default message your customers see in their email when you send estimates through Wave. Learn how to customize your email message templates.
Click Add recipient to send the estimate to multiple contacts. If you already have multiple emails associated with your customer’s profile, select one of the emails from the drop-down menu. If not, enter a new email address into the additional field.

To hide the grand total in the customer email, uncheck the box next to Show grand total in the email.
Select the checkboxes at the bottom to send a copy of the estimate to yourself, or attach the estimate as a PDF.

chunks.title: Send an estimate through Wave

chunks.title: Fix duplicate customer profiles
chunks.content:
If you accidentally create duplicate customer profiles or import a file with duplicate customer information, you can delete the unnecessary profile. However, before doing so, you need to reassign any invoices associated with that customer profile to a different customer profile. If you have paid invoices, you need to remove the payment first before you can change the customer.
If an invoice was paid through Wave's online payment feature, you cannot reassign it to a different customer. However, you can rename a customer profile to avoid using it on future invoices. To do so, follow step 1 below.
Here's how to fix duplicate customer profiles:
Step 1: Review and rename the customer profile you want to delete
On the left-side menu, click Sales & Payments > Customers.
Use the search field at the top to search for the customer by name.
Open each customer profile and click on the Invoices tab at the top to view all of their invoices. This will help you identify which profile to keep and which to delete.
Once you've identified the one to delete, click Edit customer at the top right if you're viewing the profile (or click the dropdown arrow beside the customer on the Customers page and select Edit).
Change the name in the Customer field. You can rename the profile to something like Customer name (old).
Scroll down and click Save.
The name change will be reflected across all invoices associated with this profile.
Step 2: Edit invoices to reassign to the correct customer
Click on each invoice under the customer profile you want to delete.
If an invoice is marked as paid, remove the payment before following the steps below. In the Get paid section, click Remove payment, then confirm.
Click Edit invoice.
Under the customer details section, click Choose a different customer.
Select the correct customer profile from the list.
If you remove any payments from the invoices, make sure to mark them as paid again.
Step 3: Delete the duplicate profile

chunks.title: Fix duplicate customer profiles
chunks.content: Once you’ve reassigned all invoices to the correct profile, you can delete the old customer profile. Learn how to delete a customer.

chunks.title: Add a tag to a transaction
chunks.content:
Tags are part of Wave’s Pro Plan subscription. To learn more or subscribe, see Activate a Pro Plan subscription. Tags are rolling out to businesses over the next several weeks.
Adding a tag to a transaction allows you to track that transaction as part of a specific group within your business. This allows you to see more detailed reporting. Tags can be added to both income and expense transactions.
At this time, tags are only available on the web version of Wave.
Add a tag to a transaction
Add a tag to a split transaction
Add a tag to a journal entry
Add a tag to a transaction
You can add multiple tags to a transaction. To add a tag to a transaction:
Open the Transactions page.
Create or open a transaction.
In the pop-up, under Tags, enter the name of your tag and select it from the dropdown menu. Or, enter a new tag name and click Add tag name.
Click Save.
Add a tag to a split transaction
When you split a transaction, you can add tags to each different split. Each split can have multiple tags. To add a tag to a split transaction:
Open the Transactions page.
Create or open a transaction.
In the pop-up, click Split transaction.
For each split, on the right-hand side, click the three dots, then select Add tags.
Enter your tag name and select it from the dropdown menu. Or, enter a new tag name and click Add tag name.
Click Save.
Add a tag to a journal entry
When you create a journal entry, you can add a tag to each line item. Each line item can have multiple tags. To add a tag to a journal entry:
Open your Transactions page.
Create or open your journal entry.
At the far right of the item line, click the tag icon.
Enter your tag name and select it from the dropdown list.
Click Save.

chunks.title: View and understand your tag comparison report
chunks.content:
Tags are rolling out to businesses over the next several weeks. The tag comparison report is only available on the web version of Wave.
View your tag comparison report
Understand your tag comparison report
View your tag comparison report
To view your tag comparison report:
Open the Reports page.
In the Tags section, click Tag comparison.
Select a pre-selected date range from the drop-down menu, or enter a custom date range.
Select your report type.
Choose the tags to compare. You can select up to 7 tags at one time.
Click Update report.
To remove selected tags from your current report, click the X beside their label, then click Update report.
You can also view your report from the Tags page. At the top right, click View report to open the tag comparison report.
Understand your tag comparison report
The tag comparison report allows you to see a side-by-side comparison of the income and expenses of multiple tags for a specific time period.
At the top of the report, review the net profit of each tag and the total net profit of all tags combined.
Each column in the report represents a tag. The report is divided into sections to show income, cost of goods sold, and expenses. Each section has the relevant accounts from your Chart of Accounts that your tagged transactions are categorized under. At the far right of each line is the total amount of all selected tags for that category.
Asset, liability, and equity accounts are not included in the comparison report.
Beneath the income sections, the gross profit for each selected tag is displayed. At the bottom of the report, the net profit for each selected tag is displayed.

chunks.title: Bookkeep a chargeback through Wave’s online payments
chunks.content:
The Wave Payments account and the Payments by Wave account are different versions of the same account. You may see one or both of them in your Wave account.
When you receive a chargeback on an invoice payment made through Wave’s online payments feature, the invoice cannot be deleted. To keep your books accurate and account for the chargeback withdrawal amount, there are four steps you must take:
Step 1: Record the chargeback transaction
Step 2: Record the chargeback fee
Step 3: Categorize the bank transfer
Step 4: Reconcile the Wave Payments account
Step 1: Record the chargeback transaction
To start, record the chargeback transaction:
Open your Transactions page.
Create a withdrawal transaction.
For the Date, select the date the chargeback occurred.
For the Account, select Wave Payments or Payments by Wave.
For the Category, select the related invoice.
For the Amount, enter the amount of the chargeback.
Click Save.
Step 2: Record the chargeback fee
When you receive a chargeback, there is an associated fee. To record the fee:
Open your Transactions page.
Create a withdrawal transaction.
For the Date, select the date the chargeback occurred.
For the Account, select Wave Payments or Payments by Wave.
For the Category, select Chargeback fee. If you do not have this account, create one in your Chart of Accounts.
For the Amount, enter the amount of the fee.
Click Save.
Step 3: Categorize the bank transfer
Open your Transactions page.
Find the withdrawal transaction for the chargeback. If the payment was combined with other invoice payments, the amount may be different from what you expect.
Categorize the transfer transaction to the Wave Payments or Payments by Wave clearing account. You don't need to split the transaction if it includes multiple payments.
Step 4: Reconcile the Payments by Wave clearing account
Reconcile your Payments by Wave clearing account to help ensure your books remain accurate. To reconcile this account:
Create a reconciliation period.

chunks.title: Bookkeep a chargeback through Wave’s online payments
chunks.content:
Enter the date of your last deposit, or the last day of the month, and a closing balance of $0.
Match the invoice payments that have already been deposited to your bank, and match the corresponding bank transfers. If there are invoice payments that haven’t been deposited yet, leave them unmatched.
Once the balance is $0, end the reconciliation period.

chunks.title: Automated bookkeeping with auto-updates
chunks.content:
This feature is available with a Pro Plan or Receipts subscription, or if you have a legacy business auto-importing transactions as of May 1, 2024.
Once every 24 hours, Wave automatically categorizes your bank-imported expenses and merges certain duplicate transactions to keep your books accurate. Any auto-updates that Wave makes are highlighted on your Transactions page.
Auto-updates cannot be turned off.
How auto-categorization works
How auto-merge works
How auto-categorization works
Wave categorizes expenses imported from your bank connection based on the transaction description and your past activity. If a transaction is incorrectly categorized or left uncategorized, you can categorize or recategorize the transaction.
Income transactions and transactions imported via statement uploads are not automatically categorized.
Learn how to Review auto-updates to your transactions.
How auto-merge works
Wave merges duplicate transactions when you manually mark a bill or invoice as paid, or you upload a receipt, and a matching transaction with the same account and amount is imported from your bank connection or statement upload.
If an imported transaction has multiple potential matches, to avoid an error, Wave will not merge it. Learn how to manually merge duplicate transactions. If transactions were incorrectly merged, you can unmerge them.
If a merged transaction has a receipt attached, the image remains attached. Click the Receipt icon to the right of the transaction to view the image.
Learn how to Review auto-updates to your transactions.

chunks.title: Categorize or recategorize transactions
chunks.content:
Categorizing transactions in Wave allows you to track your income and expenses under specific accounts in your reports. If a transaction isn’t categorized, it will show as an Uncategorized Income or Uncategorized Expense. Learn more about reports in Understanding your Reports page.
With a Pro Plan subscription, Wave automatically categorizes imported expense transactions. To learn about auto-categorization, see Automated bookkeeping with auto-updates.
Categorize or recategorize a transaction in your web browser
Categorize or recategorize a transaction in the Wave mobile app
Categorize or recategorize a transaction in your web browser

Locate the transaction.
Click the Category field and select an account from the dropdown menu. To create a new account, click Add a new category.
Categorize or recategorize a transaction in the Wave mobile app
Accounting transactions in the mobile app are included in Wave’s Pro and Receipts Plans. Learn about Wave’s plans.
Log in to the Wave mobile app.
On the bottom menu, tap Accounting > Transactions.
Tap on the transaction.
Tap Add category, then select a category from the list. To create a new category, tap the + icon at the top right.
Tap Save.
Newly created accounts will appear in your Chart of Accounts in the web browser version of Wave.

chunks.title: Manually merge transactions
chunks.content:
Merging transactions is only possible in the web version of Wave.
If you have duplicate transactions, you can merge them into one. You can only merge two transactions at a time. If merging the transactions will affect a completed reconciliation period, a warning pop-up will appear. Learn how to fix an unreconciled period.
To merge two transactions:
On the left-side menu, click Accounting > Transactions.
Find the two transactions you want to merge.
Select the checkboxes to the left of both transactions.
Click the merge icon.
If two transactions are merged by mistake, you can unmerge the transactions.

chunks.title: Frequently asked questions about Instant Payouts
chunks.content:
Instant payouts allow you to receive payments almost instantly, even on weekends and holidays. This feature is available through Wave's online payments feature once you meet the eligibility criteria. Below are answers to common questions about instant payouts.
If you’re using Wave's online payments feature, Wave enables instant payouts automatically when you become eligible. Wave determines eligibility based on a series of criteria, and no additional signup is required. When you become eligible for instant payouts, Wave notifies you by email.
How can I tell if I’m eligible for instant payouts?
Once eligible, your instant payout balance will appear in your account. On the left-side menu, click Banking > Payouts to view your balance or receive a payout.
How do I set up my debit card for instant payouts?
Click on your business name at the top right and select Business settings.
On the Settings menu, select Banking > Payouts.
Enter card details:
For the United States: Provide your Visa or Mastercard debit card details, along with the address on file with your bank.
For Canada: Enter your Visa Debit card details or use RBC and TD debit cards with a PLUS logo.
Why do I get an error message when adding my card?
There may be a compatibility issue with your card.
For the US: Wave supports most Visa and Mastercard debit cards
For Canada: Wave supports most Visa Debit cards as well as RBC and TD debit cards
If your card is not accepted, consider using a card from a different bank, or contact your bank for more information.
Why do I have to provide my debit card number for instant payouts if Wave already has my bank account details?
Wave requires your debit card number because it utilizes card networks (Visa and Mastercard in the US, and Visa and PLUS in Canada) for instant fund transfers, unlike standard payouts that use bank account numbers.
How is the instant payout fee calculated?

chunks.title: Frequently asked questions about Instant Payouts
chunks.content:
If your customer pays you $1,000 by credit card, the processing fee of 2.9% + 60 cents is deducted, leaving you with $970.40. The instant payout fee is 1% of this amount, totalling $9.70. After this fee, you would receive $960.70.
Will my debit card be charged?
The instant payout fee is deducted from your payout amount, so there will be no separate charge to your debit card.
How long before the money arrives in my bank account? Is it really instant?
Most banks support instant funding and you can expect to see funds in your account within seconds. However, it may take up to 30 minutes with some banks.
How do I update my debit card for instant payouts?
Click on your business name at the top right corner, then select Business settings. Under Payouts, you can update your card information at any time.
What's the minimum amount that I can take as an instant payout?
You must have a minimum balance of $25 to accept an instant payout.
I have upcoming payouts and had an available instant payout balance earlier, but it now shows $0. Why?
Every day at 8 p.m. Eastern, Wave processes payments received in the past 24 hours. If your balance shows $0, it may be due to daily processing or payment cutoffs.
For example, if you receive a payment before 8 p.m. Eastern on a Monday, you have until 3 p.m. Eastern on Tuesday to withdraw your available balance. If you receive a payment after 8 p.m Eastern on a Monday, this would process on Tuesday to be available until Wednesday at 3 p.m Eastern.
The only exception is if a payment is received after 8 p.m. Eastern on Thursday as payments don’t process on weekends. You have until 8 p.m. Eastern on Sunday to accept this instant payout.
Will all invoice payments be eligible for instant payouts?
Not all invoice payments qualify for instant payouts. If you don’t see an available balance, your payment will follow standard processing times.
What if I forget to accept an instant payout?

chunks.title: Frequently asked questions about Instant Payouts
chunks.content:
You can automate the acceptance of instant payouts based on a scheduled time. If you have an available balance, funds will be sent automatically at your pre-set time. Learn how to Schedule automatic instant payouts.
How do I bookkeep instant payouts?
Wave automatically manages the bookkeeping for instant payouts. Learn more about this feature in Automated bookkeeping with online payments.
What if I have an issue with an instant payout?
If you encounter issues, open Mave, Wave’s automated chatbot, and type "I haven’t received my instant payout." Mave will help you gather relevant details and direct you to support resources. Learn how to open Mave in Get support with Wave.

chunks.title: Troubleshoot errors with pages in your Wave account
chunks.content:
If you’re having trouble viewing or accessing certain pages or sections of your Wave account, there are a few steps you can take to troubleshoot the issue:
1. Check Wave’s status page
Wave has a status page that lists all ongoing issues that may be affecting your Wave account. The status page is updated frequently and has a daily history of software activities.
To access the status page through your Wave account:
From a web browser, open waveapps.com.
Scroll down to the bottom of the page.
Under Support & Tools, click System status.
2. Troubleshoot your browser
If there are no active incidents or outages posted on the status page, you may be experiencing an issue related to your browser or device. Ensure you are using the latest version of our supported browsers or the latest version of the Wave mobile app.
For help troubleshooting your browser, see What browsers does Wave support?
3. Contact our Support Team
If there are no active incidents or outages posted on the status page, and troubleshooting your browser did not resolve your issue, our Support Team can help. To reach them, open Mave, Wave’s automated chatbot, and request to speak with a Support Agent. Our Support Team may request screenshots of the error or to collaborate on your account to recreate the issue.

chunks.title: Frequently asked questions about invoicing
chunks.content:
Why can’t you delete some invoices?
If an invoice was paid through Wave's online payment feature, the invoice cannot be deleted, even if it has been refunded. This is to maintain an accurate record of the payment transaction. It is recommended to write off invoices if you don’t expect them to get paid. Take a look at the detailed steps to write off an invoice.
Can you recover deleted invoices?
Deleted invoices cannot be recovered. If you wish to retain them for your records, make sure to export the invoices before deleting them.
Can you delete or edit invoices in bulk?
You cannot edit or delete invoices in bulk. This is to prevent any accidental changes, as you cannot undo these actions.
Can you add late fees to an invoice?
Wave does not have a feature that automatically adds a late fee or interest to your invoice once it’s past the due date. However, you can edit the invoice in these situations to include it. Edit the invoice to add a new line item, name it something like Late fees, and enter the amount. Once you’re done, make sure to resend the invoice to your customer.
Can you edit a paid invoice to update the customer?
If a payment was recorded on an invoice, you cannot edit it to choose a different customer. If the invoice was not paid through Wave's online payment feature, you can remove the payment first. You will then be able to edit the invoice to choose a different customer, after which you can record the payment once again.
To remove a payment:
Log in to your Wave account at waveapps.com.
Navigate to Sales & Payments > Invoices, click on the invoice to view it, then click Remove payment within the Get paid section.
Can you edit an invoice number?
When you create a new invoice, Wave will automatically assign an invoice number based on the last invoice you created. For example, if the last invoice you created was 007, the next one will be 008. You can edit this as long as the invoice number is unique and not associated with another invoice.

chunks.title: Frequently asked questions about invoicing
chunks.content:
Can you add a DBA name to an invoice?
When creating an invoice, enter the DBA name in the Summary field below the invoice title. Or, include it in the Notes section of the invoice. Only this invoice will be updated. To save a default subheading or note on all invoices, customize your invoices.
Can you remove the invoice footer?
To remove the Wave footer, turn this setting off in your default invoice settings. This feature is only available to Pro Plan subscribers.

chunks.title: View your payouts
chunks.content:
What is a payout?
View your payouts
What is a payout?
A payout is the funds transferred from Wave to your bank account. A payout equals the total customer payments minus any processing fees and instant payouts.
View your payouts

Refunds issued

chunks.title: Understand how your customer can pay an invoice through Wave
chunks.content:
Make an invoice payment
Make a deposit payment
Make an invoice payment
When you send an invoice through Wave, your customer receives an email with the subject line "Invoice # from [business name]." The email provides a summary of the amount due and the due date. If online payments are enabled, the email includes a Review & Pay button that allows them to view and pay the invoice.
To make a payment, your customer must:
Click the Review & Pay button. Customers are then directed to a page with the payment options activated for that invoice.
Choose the payment method; Credit or debit card or Bank payment (EFT).
For credit card payments, customers can enter their payment information on a secure page, or use Apple Pay.
For EFTs, customers can search their bank’s name and are directed to a secure page to log in to their bank’s online banking portal.
Click Pay.
If there is an error when processing an invoice payment through Wave, our Support Team can help. Open Mave, Wave’s automated chatbot, and type human support customer payment declined. Provide the invoice number, amount of the payment, and the error message.
Make a deposit payment
When a customer has an estimate with a deposit, they receive an email titled “Estimate # from [business name].” The email provides a summary of the amount due and the due date.
To review and pay a deposit, your customer must:
Open the email and click View estimate.
Then, depending on whether the deposit is required:
To accept a deposit without an estimate, click Accept.
To accept and make a deposit payment, click Accept and pay deposit.
To make a required deposit payment, click Pay deposit.
In the payment pop-up window, enter their credit card details.
Click Pay.
If there is an error when processing a deposit payment through Wave, our Support Team can help. Open Mave, Wave’s automated chatbot, and type human support estimate deposit declined. Provide the estimate number, amount of the payment, and the error message.
